body.translated_text: <s>Vinayasūtra</s> (Aphorisms on Monastic Discipline)
[1. Chapter on Going Forth (<s>Pravrajyāvastu</s>)]
[(i) Guidance toward the status of a novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>)]
Homage to the Omniscient One.

children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Guṇaprabha</s> composed these
aphorisms (<s>sūtras</s>) of the <s>Vinaya</s> (Monastic Discipline); this is the commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on them, which is now expounded.

body.text:
tatredamādisūtram (1) atha niryāṇavṛttam // athetiśabdo 'dhikārārtham / āsūtrasaṃdarbhaparisamāpterniryāṇavṛttamadhikṛtaṃ veditavyam / prāptiratrayānaṃ, na gamanam / niryāṇaṃ yāti niryāṇaṃ niryāti aneneti / tadyathā - grāmaṃ prāptaṃ i[tivat / niḥ-śabdo 'punarāvartanakhyāpanārtham / apunarāvartakaṃ yānaṃ niryāṇa]miti śeṣaḥ / nirūpadhiśeṣanirvāṇaprāpteruktiḥ / tadvā apunarāvarttakaṃ yānam? / atha kimiti / niryānti taditi niryāṇamiti / anena śabdena sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇaprāptiḥ atroktā iti na gamyate / niryāti anena iti vā mārgo 'bhihita iti [cet], 'yasmānna niḥśabdo upakramaṇārthamāgataḥ, [nāpi paryantārthaṃ / etadāśritya sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇo]ktiḥ // saṃsāravṛttasyopakramabhūtaṃ ato yānaṃ niryāṇaṃ, paryantagamanaṃ saṃsāravṛttasya vā iti, sa ca nāśritaḥ / kiṃ tarhi apunarāvṛttyartho niḥśabdo 'tra abhīṣṭaḥ / tena yadevāpunarāvarttakaṃ yānaṃ tasyaivānenoktiḥ, nānyasya / yataśca yāṃ samāpattikakṣā[māgamya vajropamāyā anantaraṃ sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇasaṃprāptiḥ] // tatkakṣāto yad vyutthānena kakṣāntare gamanaṃ na sā na punarāvṛttiḥ / arhatvāditaḥ parihāṇiḥ sā antardhānameva // mārgasya punaḥ prāptiratra yānam, na gamanamiti // [tasmāt] gamanārthāsaṃśrayādapi niryāṇatvāprasaṅgaḥ // niryāṇagāmivṛttaṃ niryāṇavṛttam // vṛttaṃ punaratredaṃ dharmakāṇāṃ [mudrā / yadvṛttaṃ tadaśeṣataḥ vinayena proktaṃ veditavyam / tato 'trapravra]jyā vibhaṅga-poṣadha-varṣa-pravāraṇā-kaṭhina-cīvara-carma-bhaiṣajya-karma-pratikriyā-kālākālasaṃpāta-bhūmyantarasthacaraṇa-parikarma-karmabheda-cakrabheda-adhikaraṇa-śayanāsanavastu-ityanenānukrameṇa kṛtsnasya vinayavidheḥ saṃniveśanam / yasmāt ayamatra abhisaṃdhiḥ - nyā[yyā etena vidhinā pravrajyopasaṃpadoḥ upalabdhiḥ / 'eteṣāṃ ca evaṃvidhānāṃ] ceha saṃgrahaḥ, evaṃvidhāścātra varjyāḥ / ityasya pūrvaṃ vaktuṃ yogaḥ iti ādau pravrajyāvastunaḥ saṃniveśanam / śāsane praviṣṭasya anupete 'tra vṛtte śikṣāniḥ kṣepaṇādinā iyaṃ śikṣā / ityato 'nantaraṃ vibhaṅgasya [saṃniveśanam] // poṣadhavastvādīnāmapi imānyatra kramakāraṇāni - paripoṣaṇaṃ yathā samāttāyā śi[kṣāyā kāle-kāle sūtramāśritya / tasmāt poṣadhāvastu abhihi]tam // yasmin kāle ekatrāvasthānena arthasaṃpattiḥ tadavasthānagatau vidhiḥ ityato varṣavastu

) saṃghaṃ pravārayāmīti śuddhau satyāṃ utsargadānasya yujyamānatā ityato 'nantaraṃ pravāraṇāvastu // vyūhabandhaḥ kaścidasya varṣāvasātmano [niyatavāsasya prati-kañcukabhūtaḥ vidyate / prasrabdhivihāritārthaṃ avalambanīyaḥ / asya anantaraṃ tasya kramaḥ iti kaṭhinavastu niveśitam // pṛthaktatra nāpattau cīvaravibhāgasya yogaḥ iti apagatattvena tayoḥ vyūhabandhayo cīvaradānasya kālaḥ iti cīvaravidheḥ āśrayaṇam / cīvaraprabhedabhūtaṃ jñānaṃ carmaṃ ityatonantaraṃ carmavastu [niveśitam] // na vinā rogapratīkāreṇa eka(ḥ) pṛthagvā vihartu śakyata i[ti sahapratyā] sannābhyāṃ pūrvāparakālābhyāṃ pratha(ma)meva cīvaradānakāle prāyaśo glānyā pātasya bhāvaḥ / tadgato 'smāt pratikriyāvidhiyuktarūpa iti bhaiṣajyavastu // utpannotpanneṣu evaṃ viharatāṃ karaṇīyesu anuṣṭhānavidhiḥ, ityatonantaraṃ karmavastu // udvṛttānāṃ praṇidhikarmārhādīnāṃ praṇidhikarmakaraṇādinā niyamanaṃ pratyāpādanaṃ ca avasāraṇādinā yuktamityataḥ pratikriyāvastu // āpannasaṃghāvaśeṣasya ca kālākālasaṃpāta-bhūmyantarasthacaraṇavastunoḥ niyamanapratyāpādanārthaṃ saṃniveśanam / kauśāmbaka-pāṇdulohitaka-pudgalaparivāsikavastūni pratikriyāvastvādi nāmabhiḥ uktāni / saṃjñāntaraniveśanaprayojanaṃ tatraiva krame vakṣyāmaḥ // niyamanādau anupatiṣṭhatāṃ paridamanaṃ yuktarūpamityataḥ parikarmavastu // [poṣadha]sthāpanavastunaḥ etatsaṃjñāntaraṃ vakṣyamāṇārthaṃ dvaidhagateṣu vṛttamityetatkarmacakrabhedavastunī // vyavahāragato vidhiḥ ato 'nantaraṃ yujyate / ityasmādadhikaraṇavastu // yatraitad sarvaṃ anyaśca kuśalapakṣo 'nuṣṭhīyate sthāne, tadgato 'smādvidhiḥ yukta iti śayanāsanavastu niveśitam // kṣudrakādīnāṃ caitad - prabhedabhūtatvāt anatireka ebhyaḥ iti na pṛthaksūtraṇam // yatra yasya yogaḥ tatastatraiva niveśitam / ācāryopādhyāhyānujñānāt [anantaraṃ] yaḥ pravrajyopanayavidhiḥ tadupadarśanārthamāha - (2) sarvasmin sannipatite saṃghe kṛtedaveṣaṃ nipatya pragṛhītāñjaliṃ utkuṭukasthaṃ vṛddhānte yācitavantaṃ trirjñapticaturthena karmaṇā saha pravrajyopasaṃpadau upanayeyuḥ iti purā-kalpaḥ // maṇḍalake saṃghaikadeśasannipātapratiṣedhārthaṃ sarvasmin iti vacanam // na maṇḍalakasthe 'pi saṃghai(ka)deśe, kiṃtarhi tadantasīmānivāsini sarvasmin // kṛto 'yaṃ veṣo 'nena iti
kṛtedaṃveṣāḥ // ayamiti buddhaśāsanabhikṣuveṣāpadeśaḥ / apanītakeśaśmaśruṃ bhikṣuveṣaṃ ca prāvṛtricīvaraṃ ityarthaḥ / nipatya iti vṛddhānta iti yadvakṣyate, tasya cābhisaṃbandhaḥ / vṛddhānte nipatya pañcamaṇḍalakena vandanāṃ kṛtvā ityarthaḥ // pragṛhītāñjalimiti kṛtāñjalim // utkuṭukasthamiti utkuṭukikayā 'vasthitam / nāsanopaviṣṭam / kvāvasthitamityāha vṛddhānte // nanū niṣaṇṇasya utkuṭukikayā vṛddhānte pragṛhītāñjalitvaṃ ityetatsaṃghādhīne karmaṇi-paribhāṣāyāṃ sarvakarmādhikārikaṃ sūtritam / tata eva ihāpi karmatvāt asya tritayasya prāptau satyāṃ (
children.translated_text: At the end of the rains-retreat, which consists of a fixed dwelling, [the monk says] 'I invite the <s>Saṅgha</s> by three grounds — by what has been seen, etc.' — when purity exists, the propriety of giving the release (<s>utsarga</s>) — therefore the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation) chapter follows next. There is a certain structure (<s>vyūhabandha</s>) that serves as a protective sheath for this fixed dwelling of the rains-retreat; it is to be relied upon for the purpose of comfortable dwelling. Its chapter follows next — thus the <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-frame) chapter is placed. Since the distribution of robes is proper separately when there is no [kaṭhina-related] offense — because the time for giving robes is when those two structures have been completed — therefore the robe (<s>cīvara</s>) procedure follows. Since leather is a subdivision of robes, therefore the leather (<s>carma</s>) chapter is placed next. Since one cannot dwell, either together or separately, without remedying illness — and since illness usually occurs at the time of robe-giving, in both the earlier and later periods — and since a remedy is appropriate for that — therefore the medicine (<s>bhaiṣajya</s>) chapter. The procedure for performance in matters of conduct that arise while living thus — therefore the formal acts (<s>karma</s>) chapter follows next. The restraining by remedial acts and so forth of those who have transgressed, who deserve disciplinary action and so forth, and the rehabilitation by reinstatement and so forth is proper — therefore the remedies (<s>pratikriyā</s>) chapter. The chapter on timely and untimely occurrences and inter-regional conduct is arranged for the purpose of restraining and rehabilitating one who has committed a <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> (offense entailing a formal meeting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>). The <s>Kauśāmbaka</s>, <s>Pāṇḍulohitaka</s>, and <s>Pudgalapārivāsika</s> chapters are named as remedies chapters under different names. The purpose of establishing different nomenclature will be explained in [its proper] place in the sequence. Since disciplining those who do not comply during the restraining procedure and so forth is proper — therefore the preparatory acts (<s>parikarma</s>) chapter. The <s>poṣadha</s>-suspension chapter under a different name, for the purpose to be explained — the conduct when there is a twofold division — these are the division of acts and division of the circle chapters. The procedure regarding legal proceedings — therefore the legal disputes (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>) chapter follows next. The rule regarding the place where all this and other wholesome practices are performed — since that rule is proper, therefore the lodgings (<s>śayanāsanavastu</s>) chapter is placed. As for the minor rules (<s>kṣudraka</s>) and others — since they are subdivisions [of these topics], they are not excessive beyond these; therefore there is no separate formulation. Where each is appropriate, it is placed there. After the authorization of the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) and preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), for the purpose of demonstrating the procedure of guidance toward ordination, he says: (2) 'When the entire <s>Saṅgha</s> has assembled, one who has put on the [monastic] attire, having prostrated, with joined palms, squatting, at the senior end, after making the request three times, should be admitted to both going forth and full ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s> and <s>upasaṃpad</s>) by a formal act with a motion and three proclamations (<s>jñapticaturtha karma</s>) — this is the ancient rule (<s>purākalpa</s>).' The word 'entire' (<s>sarvasmin</s>) is to prohibit the assembly of merely a portion of the <s>Saṅgha</s> in the consecrated area (<s>maṇḍalaka</s>). Not merely a portion of the <s>Saṅgha</s> present in the consecrated area, but rather all those dwelling within its boundaries. 'One who has put on this attire' (<s>kṛtedaṃveṣa</s>) means one who has adopted the appearance of a monk in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching — meaning one whose hair and beard have been removed and who has put on the monastic attire of the triple robe (<s>tricīvara</s>). 'Having prostrated' connects with what will be said [next]: 'at the senior end.' Having prostrated at the senior end with the five-point prostration — that is the meaning. 'With joined palms' (<s>pragṛhītāñjali</s>) means with hands folded. 'Squatting' (<s>utkuṭukastha</s>) means standing in the squatting posture, not seated on a seat. Where standing? — he says: 'at the senior end.' Now, [the requirements of] squatting at the senior end with joined palms for one who is seated — these have been formulated in the general rules for all acts under the topic of <s>Saṅgha</s>-governed formal acts. Since this too is a formal act, when these three [conditions] are already established from that [general rule],

) kimiti punarvacanam - 'vartamānakalpādhikārikatvāt pragṛhītāñjali' mityādeḥ paribhāṣāto astyasyeha purākalpe siddhiritivacanam // yācitavantamiti kim / pravrajyopasaṃpadau / yācanaṃ punaḥ - "śṛṇotu, bhadantāḥ saṃgho, ahamevaṃnāmā ākāṅkṣāmisvākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyopasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam" iti vistaraḥ // anena mantreṇa triryācitavantaṃ jñapticaturthena karmaṇā iti tisro vācanā jñapticaturthā yasmin karmaṇi tad jñapticaturthaṃ karma, tena // sahapravrajyopasaṃpadau iti pravrajyopasaṃpacca samānakālaṃ, na krameṇeti // upanayeyuriti saṃghabhūtā bhikṣavaḥ // tathā ca mantraḥ"śṛṇotu, bhadantāḥ saṃgho, ayamevaṃnāmā ākāṃkṣati svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāmupasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ yāvat prāvrājita upasaṃpādita evaṃnāmā saṃgheneti" // iti purākalpaḥ // iti-śabdaḥ prakāravācī // purākalpa iti vartamānakalpāt prāk evaṃ-prakāraḥ pravrajyopasaṃpadvidhirityarthaḥ // atha kimiti vartamānakalpa eva bhagavatā na prākprajñaptaḥ, kiṃ nā purākalpatyāgena asya vidheḥ punaḥ prajñapanam? [iti cet], viśuddhasattvā hi te tadānīṃ pratipattāraḥ / teṣāṃ na krameṇa viniyamyatvaṃ, na parāvaṣṭaṃbhena pariśikṣaṇaṃ vā / [na] glānyameṣāṃ, kṛtapuṇyatvāt asat na saṃpadyate - 'saṃpanne vā bhavantyeṣāṃ svayamevānukampakāḥ' / āntarāyikadharmāṇāṃ tadānīṃ anāpatteḥ / tathā 'pasartṝṇāṃ ityataḥ purākalpaprajñapanam / yadā tvanyavidhā apyete jātāḥ tadottarasya saṃprattaṃ naiva kaścidupayogaḥ / kimanenehopanibaddhena? yadyapyanena kalpenā[dhunā] 'vyavahāraḥ,
tathāpi nāstyasyottarādanyatvaṃ, parikaramātrakaṃ tadasya yaduttaratra viśeṣaḥ / tatredaṃ mantratantram / etāvanmātrakamevāsīt, dvikamevaitadāsī(t) / vinayavaśādasya aparasyātravidheḥ vyavasthā-[na]-mityāsyārthasya khyāpanārthaṃ asyopanibandhaḥ / evaṃ saprayojanaḥ purākalpa upadarśitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Why the repetitive statement? From the interpretive rule beginning with 'because it pertains to the present epoch (<s>vartamānakalpa</s>), with palms joined,' there is the statement 'there is for him accomplishment here in the former epoch (<s>purākalpa</s>).' What does 'having requested' [mean]? Ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>). The request, moreover, is: 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear! I, named so-and-so, desire ordination and full ordination, the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s>, in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>' — and so forth in detail. By this formula, having requested three times, [it is done] through an act with a motion and three proclamations (<s>jñapticaturtha karma</s>): the act in which there are three recitations along with the motion is called a <s>jñapticaturtha</s> act — by that [act]. 'Together ordination and full ordination' means ordination and full ordination occur at the same time, not sequentially. 'They should admit' means the <s>bhikṣus</s> constituting the <s>saṃgha</s>. And the formula is: 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear! This one named so-and-so desires ordination, full ordination, and the status of a <s>bhikṣu</s> in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>, up to: the one named so-and-so has been ordained and fully ordained by the <s>saṃgha</s>.' Thus is the former epoch (<s>purākalpa</s>). The word 'thus' (<s>iti</s>) denotes manner. 'Former epoch' means: prior to the present epoch, such was the procedure for ordination and full ordination — this is the meaning. Now why was this not prescribed by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the present epoch itself? Why was this procedure not re-prescribed by abandoning the former-epoch [method]? [The answer is:] Those who practiced at that time were beings of pure disposition. For them, there was no need for sequential regulation, nor training through the support of others. There was no weariness for them, because having accumulated merit, the unvirtuous does not come about — 'when [merit] is accomplished, they themselves naturally become compassionate.' Because at that time, obstructive conditions (<s>āntarāyika dharmas</s>) did not arise. And because of 'those who go forth,' therefore the former-epoch prescription [was made]. But when those of other dispositions also arose, thereafter the subsequent [procedure] has no use whatsoever. What purpose does [the former epoch] serve when it is bound here [in the text]? Although there is no current practice according to this epoch, nevertheless it is not different from the subsequent [epoch]; it is merely preparatory for the distinction that comes later. Therein lies this formula-and-procedure (<s>mantratantra</s>). Just this much alone existed; this was twofold only. By the force of the <s>Vinaya</s>, the establishment of this subsequent procedure here — the inclusion [of the former epoch] is for the purpose of making known this meaning. Thus the former epoch has been shown to be purposeful.

body.translated_text: Therein, this is the first aphorism: (1) 'Now, the conduct leading to final departure (<s>niryāṇavṛtta</s>).' The word 'now' (<s>atha</s>) indicates the commencement of a topic. From [this point] to the completion of the arrangement of aphorisms, the conduct leading to final departure should be understood as the governing subject. '<s>Niryāṇa</s>' means attainment, not going — [it is called <s>niryāṇa</s> because] one attains <s>niryāṇa</s>, one departs through this — just as one says 'arrived at the village.' The prefix 'niḥ' indicates non-return. The vehicle (<s>yāna</s>) of non-return is the rest [of the meaning of] <s>niryāṇa</s>. This refers to the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>). Or is it the vehicle of non-return? Then why [the term <s>niryāṇa</s>]? Because 'one departs by it, therefore it is <s>niryāṇa</s>' — by this word, it is not understood that the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣanirvāṇa</s>) is meant here. Or if [one says] 'that by which one departs is the path' — since the prefix 'niḥ' has not come in the sense of commencement nor in the sense of termination, this is the statement of <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder. The vehicle that is the commencement of the round of <s>saṃsāra</s> is <s>niryāṇa</s>, or the going to the end of the round of <s>saṃsāra</s> — but that [meaning] is not intended. Rather, the prefix 'niḥ' here is intended in the sense of non-return. Therefore, this statement refers only to the vehicle of non-return, not to any other. And since, upon reaching the level of attainment from which, immediately after the diamond-like [concentration] (<s>vajropamasamādhi</s>), there is the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> with remainder — the movement from that level to another level by rising [from samādhi] is not a 'return.' The fall from <s>arhatship</s> and so forth is merely a disappearance. Here, 'vehicle' means the re-attainment of the path, not going. Therefore, even from the standpoint of the meaning of 'going,' there is no implication of [it being called] <s>niryāṇa</s>. The conduct that leads to <s>niryāṇa</s> is the 'conduct of <s>niryāṇa</s>' (<s>niryāṇavṛtta</s>). The 'conduct' here is the seal (<s>mudrā</s>) of the <s>Dharma</s> holders. Whatever conduct [is prescribed], all of it should be understood as stated by the <s>Vinaya</s>. Therefore, herein the arrangement of the entire <s>Vinaya</s> procedure is in the following order: going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>), analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>), observance (<s>poṣadha</s>), rains-retreat (<s>varṣa</s>), invitation (<s>pravāraṇā</s>), <s>kaṭhina</s> (robe-material), robes (<s>cīvara</s>), leather (<s>carma</s>), medicine (<s>bhaiṣajya</s>), formal acts (<s>karma</s>), remedies (<s>pratikriyā</s>), timely and untimely occurrences (<s>kālākālasaṃpāta</s>), inter-regional conduct (<s>bhūmyantarasthacaraṇa</s>), preparatory acts (<s>parikarma</s>), division of acts (<s>karmabheda</s>), division of the circle (<s>cakrabheda</s>), legal disputes (<s>adhikaraṇa</s>), and lodgings (<s>śayanāsanavastu</s>). Since the intention here is: 'Legitimate is the obtaining of going forth and full ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s> and <s>upasaṃpad</s>) by this procedure. And those of this type are compiled here, and those of this type are to be excluded here.' Since it is proper to state this first, the chapter on going forth is placed first. For one who has entered the [Buddha's] teaching, when this conduct is not followed, this is the training — by means of expulsion from the training and so forth; therefore, the chapter on analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) is placed next. The reasons for the sequential order of the <s>poṣadha</s> chapter and so forth are as follows: The nourishment (<s>paripoṣaṇa</s>) of the training that has been undertaken, from time to time, based on the aphorism — therefore the <s>poṣadha</s> chapter is stated. At the time when accomplishment of purpose is achieved by dwelling together in one place, the rule regarding that dwelling — therefore the rains-retreat (<s>varṣa</s>) chapter.

) tataḥ pariśuddhāyāsmai pūrvopādhyāyatvena śrāmaṇeropādhyāyatvena avakāśaṃ kuryāt - 'ahaṃ bhadantaṃ pravrājayāmi' iti / tathā ca granthaḥ - "yasya kasyacit pravrajyāpekṣa upasaṃkrāmati, sa tenāntarāyikān dharmān pṛṣṭa udgṛhītavya" iti / saṃvarāṇāṃ ānupūrvyaṃ darśayannāha - (5) nānupapannasya pūrvaṃ upāsakatva-śrāvaṇeratva-bhikṣutvānāmuttaram / eṣāmupāsakatvādīnāṃ pūrvaṃ-pūrvaṃ parvānupapannasya tādātmyopagatyā anupagatasya uttaraṃ uttaraṃ parva na kāryam / vyavasthākhyānametad // pṛṣṭvā āntarāyikān pravrajyāpekṣaṃ ādāvupāsakatvaṃ grāhayet, tataḥ śrāmaṇeratvaṃ, tato bhikṣutvaṃ bhavati ityasya bodhanārthaṃ / na tvetadarthaṃ pūrvasminnasamāttena bhavatyuttarasya rūḍhiriti // bhikṣusaṃvarasya pūrvaṃ saṃvarāntareṇāpi rūḍhau mukhyamastyeva [mūla]vacanam / śrāmaṇerasaṃvarastu upāsakasaṃvaraṃ vibhavati iti rūḍhiḥ / bhikṣusaṃvaraḥ pratiśaranaṃ na tvasti[iti] vacanam / śaraṇagamaṇapūrvakaṃ saṃvarādānamiti darśayannāha - (6) śara[ṇa]gatyabhyupaga[mavaca]nopakramaṃ upāsakatva-śrāmaṇeratvābhyupagamavacanaṃ kurvīta // gatirgamanam / śaraṇagamanasyābhyupagamaḥ śaraṇagatyabhyupagamaḥ - buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmītyādi / tadabhidhāyakaṃ vacanaṃ śaraṇagatyabhyupagamavacanam, tadvacanam / upakrama ārambhaḥ / upāsakatva-śrāmaṇeratvābhyupagamavacanaṃ kurvīta // ko 'sau? pratīpattā, ayamarthaḥ / evaṃ samādātrā vaktavyam - "sāmanvāhara bhadanta ahaṃ evaṃnāmā buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi yāvat gaṇānāmagryam, upāsakaṃ māṃ bhadanto dhārayatu yāvajjīvam, samanvāhara bhadanta ahamevaṃnāmā buddhaṃ yāvat gaṇānāmagryaṃ / śrāmaṇeraṃ māṃ ācāryo dhārayatu //" evaṃ bhūtāveva saṃdarbhau triḥ āvartayitavyau // ye[na]tu ke[na]ciccharaṇagamanaṃ ādau trirāvartya tataḥ paścādupāsakaṃ māṃ bhadanto dhārayatu, śrāmaṇeraṃ māmācārya ityabhidhīyate, so 'sau vedayitavyaḥ // - yasmādanayoḥ saṃvarasamādānavacasoḥ, evaṃ sati, śaraṇagamanoktiḥ naiva aṅgabhāvaṃ pratipadyate / kiñca yena prāgeva śaraṇagamanamātraṃ [abhyupagamyate] tasya saṃvarādānakāle śaraṇagamanasyāvacanīyatāpattiḥ
// avaśyaṃ caitad nirvāṇāśayaprarūpaṇārthaṃ asminkāle vaktavyam / evam hyetad saṃvarasamādānavacasoḥ aṅgaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavati, nānyathā / na ca nirvāṇāśaya-dārḍhyamantareṇa saṃvarasyotthānam // yasmāt nirvāṇānuguṇyaḥ saṃvaraḥ, upasaṃpadastarhi śaraṇagamanavacanamantareṇa kathaṃ rūḍhiḥ? naiṣa doṣaḥ / upasaṃpacchabdādeva tadarthasiddheḥ / sarvākaranīyaviratilakṣaṇatvāt, sarvātmanā hi nirvāṇopagatiḥ upasaṃpad / yataḥ upasaṃpadi sthitaḥ nirvāṇānuguṇyo vyavasthito bhavati // kurvīta ityātmanepadaṃ pratipattyā etat karanīyaṃ ityetatsaṃdarśanārtham / yadatraparo 'bhidhatte śikṣaṇaṃ taditi mantavyaṃ, na dānagrahaṇam, upoṣadhe 'pi pratipatturevaitatkaraṇīyaṃ iti mantavyam / yatte dānagrahaṇadharmaḥ tatra iti kecid varṇayanti śikṣaṇādeva / bhrāntirasau teṣāmiti jñeyam, tulyatvātsamādānasya // (7) anantaramasya śikṣotkīrttanaṃ (
children.translated_text: then for the one who is pure, [the preceptor] should grant permission for the preliminary preceptorship, the <s>śrāmaṇera</s>-preceptorship, [saying]: 'I, <s>Bhadanta</s>, shall ordain you.' And the text says: 'Whoever approaches seeking ordination, he should be asked about the obstructive conditions and then accepted.' Showing the sequence of the precepts, he says — (5) For one who has not attained the prior [stage], among <s>upāsakatva</s> (lay-follower status), <s>śrāmaṇeratva</s> (novice status), and <s>bhikṣutva</s> (full monk status), the subsequent [stage should not be conferred]. For one who has not attained the prior stage among these — <s>upāsakatva</s> and the rest — by entering into identity with each successive stage, the subsequent stage should not be performed. This is a statement of systematic arrangement. Having asked about the obstructive conditions regarding ordination, one should first make [the candidate] adopt <s>upāsakatva</s> (lay-follower status), then <s>śrāmaṇeratva</s> (novice status), then <s>bhikṣutva</s> (full monk status) comes about — this is for the purpose of making this understood. But it is not the case that the subsequent [stage] is established for one who has not undertaken the prior. Even for the establishment of the <s>bhikṣu</s> precepts with a different prior precept, there is indeed a primary textual basis. The <s>śrāmaṇera</s> precepts, however, supersede the <s>upāsaka</s> precepts — this is the establishment. The <s>bhikṣu</s> precepts are the refuge; there is no statement to the contrary. Showing that the taking of precepts is preceded by going for refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>), he says — (6) One should perform the declaration of undertaking <s>upāsakatva</s> (lay-follower status) and <s>śrāmaṇeratva</s> (novice status), beginning with the words of acceptance of going for refuge. 'Going' (<s>gati</s>) means 'going' (<s>gamana</s>). The acceptance of going for refuge is <s>śaraṇagatyabhyupagama</s> — 'I go to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge' and so forth. The words expressing that are the words of acceptance of going for refuge (<s>śaraṇagatyabhyupagamavacana</s>); those are the words. 'Beginning' (<s>upakrama</s>) means commencement. One should perform the declaration of undertaking <s>upāsakatva</s> and <s>śrāmaṇeratva</s>. Who is 'one'? The practitioner — this is the meaning. Thus the one undertaking [the precepts] should say: 'Bear witness, <s>Bhadanta</s>! I, named so-and-so, go to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge, up to: the foremost of communities (<s>gaṇa</s>). May the <s>Bhadanta</s> hold me as an <s>upāsaka</s> for as long as I live. Bear witness, <s>Bhadanta</s>! I, named so-and-so, [go to] the <s>Buddha</s>, up to: the foremost of communities. May the <s>Ācārya</s> hold me as a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>.' These two passages, just as they are, should be repeated three times. But by some, the going for refuge is first repeated three times, and then afterward 'May the <s>Bhadanta</s> hold me as an <s>upāsaka</s>; may the <s>Ācārya</s> hold me as a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>' is declared — that [practice] should be recognized [as incorrect]. Because for these two declarations of undertaking precepts, in that case, the utterance of going for refuge does not attain the status of a component part. Moreover, for one who has previously accepted merely the going for refuge, at the time of taking precepts, the fault of not needing to state the going for refuge would arise. This [going for refuge] must necessarily be stated at this time for the purpose of declaring the aspiration for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For thus it becomes a component part of the declarations of undertaking precepts, not otherwise. And without firmness in the aspiration for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the precepts do not arise. Since the precepts are conducive to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, how then is full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>) established without the words of going for refuge? This is not a fault — because the meaning is accomplished by the very word <s>upasaṃpad</s>. Because [full ordination] is characterized by abstention from all that is not to be done, full ordination is the complete approach to <s>nirvāṇa</s> with one's entire being. Since one who abides in full ordination is established as conducive to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The middle voice (<s>ātmanepada</s>) in 'should perform' (<s>kurvīta</s>) is for showing that this is to be done by the practitioner. What another declares here as 'training' (<s>śikṣaṇa</s>) — that should be considered [correct], not the [interpretation as] giving and receiving. Even in the <s>upoṣadha</s> (observance day), this is to be done by the practitioner alone — this should be understood. As for what some explain as 'the procedure of giving and receiving there' — [deriving it] from 'training' (<s>śikṣaṇa</s>) alone — that is their error, it should be known, because the undertaking [of precepts] is the same [in both cases]. (7) Immediately after this comes the declaration of the training rules,

) [abhyupagamarūpeṇa] iti // asya iti upāsakatva-śrāmaṇeratvābhyupagamavacanasyānantaraṃ upāsaka-śrāmaṇerakaśikṣāyāḥ tacchikṣāpadānāṃ yathāyogamutkīrtanam / pūrvatra pañcānāṃ, uttaratra daśānām, kena prakāreṇa ityāha - abhyupagamarūpeṇa / itaśca itaśca prativiramāmi iti, no tu idaṃ cedaṃ ca rakṣyaṃ yattvayā samāttam iti // (8) svayaṃ upāsakatāṃ upanīya, ārocakāya saṃghasya arpayet bhikṣave // svayamiti prakṛtatvāt upādhyāyaḥ, sa hi tatpravrājane kṛtāvakāśaḥ / sa svayamevopāsakatāmupanīya upāsakasaṃvaraṃ dattvā / yastaṃ pravrajyāpekṣaṃ saṃghasya ārocayate, tasmai samarpayeta bhikṣave - 'ārocayaina'miti / bhikṣusaṃbandhādasyeti - kartavyatājātasya / svārthamevaitadupādhyāyasyeti pradarśanārthamātmanepadam // [jñaptyādi]-karmātmakatvādasya anupasaṃpannenāpi saṃghe pravrajyāpekṣasya ārocanaṃ na virudhyata ityasya vikalpasya vyudāsārthaṃ bhikṣave iti vacanam / tathā ca granthaḥ - tataḥ paścāt bhikṣuradhyeṣitavyaḥ - yo 'syārocayate iti // ārocako 'pi (9) 'kaccitpariśuddha' iti samarpitāramupādhyāyaṃ pṛṣtvā, śuddhaṃ santaṃ pravrajyāpekṣaṃ ārocaye[t] - "śruṇotu bhadantāḥ, saṃgho samanvāhrīyatāṃ - ayamevaṃnāmā pravrajyāpekṣo gṛhītāvadātavasanaḥ" ityādinā mantreṇārocayediti yatparasmaipadaṃ tad paravyāpāreṇāsya pravṛtterasvārthatvāt / na hi atra yathā upādhyāye putra iva pravṛtteḥ svārthatvamevāsya // kathaṃ avasthite saṃghe ārocayedityāha - (10) sarvasannipāte vā [sanniṣaṇṇe ']nulayane vā // anuparigaṇikayā ityasyedaṃ vivaraṇaṃ anulayanamiti / parigaṇo hi layanaviśeṣaḥ // yeṣāṃ saṃnidhau ārocyate teṣāṃ yo vidhiḥ taddarśayannāha - (11) sa cetpariśuddha

children.translated_text: [In the form of acceptance.] 'Of this' means: immediately after the words of acceptance of lay-follower status or novice status, the recitation of the training rules of the lay-follower's or novice's training, their respective precepts, as appropriate. For the former, five; for the latter, ten. In what manner? He says: 'in the form of acceptance' — 'I refrain from this and from this,' not 'this and that are to be guarded, which you have undertaken.' (8) Having himself led [the candidate] to the status of a lay-follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), [the preceptor] should hand him over to a <s>bhikṣu</s> who is the announcer to the <s>saṅgha</s>. 'Himself' means the preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), since the context is established; for he has been authorized in [the candidate's] ordination. Having himself conferred the lay-follower status and given the lay-follower's restraint, [the preceptor should hand] to the one who announces to the <s>saṅgha</s> the candidate seeking ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) — he should entrust him to a <s>bhikṣu</s>, saying 'announce this one.' 'Of this' refers to the one connected with a <s>bhikṣu</s>, [i.e.,] one for whom duties have arisen. The middle voice (ātmanepada) is used to show that this is for the preceptor's own purpose. In order to remove the doubt that, since this [act] has the nature of a <s>jñapti</s> (formal motion) etc., even an unordained person might make the announcement in the <s>saṅgha</s> of one seeking ordination — for this reason the word '<s>bhikṣu</s>' is used. And thus the text [states]: 'Thereafter a <s>bhikṣu</s> should be requested — one who announces for him.' (9) The announcer too, having asked the preceptor who has entrusted [the candidate], 'Is he pure?,' should announce the candidate seeking ordination when he is pure, with the formula: 'May the venerable <s>saṅgha</s> hear, may the <s>saṅgha</s> give attention — this one named so-and-so, seeking ordination, has taken the white garments' and so on. The active voice (parasmaipada) is used because this [announcing] is undertaken through the agency of another and is not for one's own purpose. For here, unlike with the preceptor, there is no self-interest as if for a son. (10) In what state should the <s>saṅgha</s> be when [the announcer] makes the announcement? He says: Either at a full assembly or when seated at a chapter (<s>anulaya</s>). 'Chapter' (<s>anulaya</s>) is the explanation of 'assembly-counting' (<s>anuparigaṇikā</s>). For a chapter (<s>parigaṇa</s>) is a particular type of <s>layana</s> (assembly). (11) Regarding the procedure for those in whose presence the announcement is made, he says: If he is pure, all should say so. 'If' is in the sense of 'when.' After the announcement, the one seeking ordination — (12) should request the preceptor with the request-formula. And the preceptor (13) should have his hair and beard shaved, except for the topknot (<s>cūḍā</s>). The middle voice is used to indicate that by establishing [someone] as preceptor, the barber's task is demonstrated [as something to be arranged]; it should not be thought that the preceptor himself must personally do this. What is caused to be done through intermediaries should not be regarded as not done, since the action is purpose-directed. Therefore, when the purpose is accomplished, the action ceases. Hence, if the hair-and-beard shaving is accomplished by another without waiting for the preceptor's personal involvement, one should not think 'the preceptor should not proceed with this.' 'Except for the topknot' means other than the topknot. [This is done so that] even in the removal of the topknot, the sense of disfigurement may not be [felt]. Therefore, to ascertain whether he is certain or not, through a question, the retention [of the topknot] is for the purpose of inquiry — (14) When asked 'Let the topknot be removed,' if [the candidate] consents, then — 'Let the topknot be removed' is what is said; when the one to be ordained, having been asked, gives consent, then upon his consent to the removal of the topknot, [the text continues] 'he should remove that topknot.' Thus with hair and beard removed, (15) he should bathe — with water appropriate to the season. After bathing, (16) the preceptor should give him the saffron-colored (<s>kāṣāya</s>) garments. And he (17) should receive them, falling at the feet of the preceptor. Then the preceptor himself (18) should [robe him].

children.translated_text: He should robe [the candidate], and while robing, in order to avoid the defects of being a eunuch (<s>ṣāṇḍha</s>), a <s>paṇḍaka</s>, one without sexual characteristics, or a hermaphrodite (<s>ubhayavyañjana</s>), (19) he should examine the sexual characteristics unobtrusively — not by making [the candidate] naked, but unobtrusively, so that the [candidate] does not know: 'My characteristics have been seen by this person.' This task belongs to the preceptor by virtue of his acceptance. [But] if done by another trusted <s>bhikṣu</s>, it should be regarded as done by the preceptor. (20) He should confer the ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), beginning with the taking of refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>). 'I, named so-and-so, [take refuge in] the <s>Buddha</s>... up to the foremost of assemblies, that <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni</s>... up to "I take up the mark of ordination"' — with this formula the preceptor should confer the ordination beginning with the taking of refuge; the meaning is that it should not be without the taking of refuge as the foundation. [Objection:] Is it not the case that the [ordination] vow follows? What purpose does the taking of refuge serve as a beginning? Some say this. That is incorrect. Because ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) means the abandonment of household attachment; all conditioned things are tainted; attachment to them is household entanglement; therefore turning away from <s>saṃsāra</s> is the completeness of the abandonment of household attachment. And the accomplishment of turning away from <s>saṃsāra</s> is not possible without reliance on <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, just as with the vow, here too the declaration of the intention toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> must be made — hence the ordination begins with the taking of refuge. Some read in the ordination formula, before 'I take up the mark of ordination,' [the words] 'May the preceptor hold me as a novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>).' That is incorrect, because what has already sprouted does not sprout again, and what has already been undertaken cannot be undertaken again, and it would be inconsistent for the teacher to read this in the formula. Some also read in the novice-ordination formula the entry into ordination: 'that <s>Bhagavān Śākyamuni</s>... up to "I take up the mark of ordination. For the sake of purpose, I take the name of the preceptor. The teacher named so-and-so, may the teacher hold me as a novice."' Since what has been undertaken cannot be undertaken again, this is inappropriate. (21) Or immediately after the request — thus 'he should confer the ordination' continues. The word 'or' indicates an alternative view. The reading of some is: 'Immediately after the request of the preceptor, with hair and beard not yet shaved, [the candidate] should be ordained.' Their view is: just as novice-status, so too the hair-shaving etc. is something done after ordination. This is the basis for the variant reading. Thus the ordination-preceptor should hand him over to (22) a <s>bhikṣu</s> who will confer novice status. The one who confers novice status upon him, whose disposition is to confer novice status — this is the 'novice-status conferrer' (<s>śrāmaṇeratvopanāyin</s>). The mental preparedness for recognizing the conferral of the novice restraint by the one who confers it — this should be understood as dependent on that disposition. The one for whose conferral [the candidate] is entrusted — he (23) having asked 'Is [the candidate] pure?,' should confer [novice status] upon the pure one. (24) He is the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>). This novice-status conferrer should be regarded as the teacher. (25) The private instructor, the action-performer, the shelter-giver, and the text-teacher are also teachers. The word 'and' is in the sense of accumulation. When are these teacher-statuses established? He says: (26) [Their teacher-status] comes into being when the purpose is fulfilled — he says: when the purpose for which the formula is established, for example the purpose of conferring novice status, is fulfilled, that is, when that purpose is concluded, the teacher-status etc. come into being — they are established. body.translated_text: The present epoch (<s>vartamānakalpa</s>) is now stated — (3) For one who has taken refuge with a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> as preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) therein, ordination and full ordination [are conferred]. 'A certain <s>bhikṣu</s>' — the word 'certain' (<s>kaṃcit</s>) is used to indicate that it is not necessarily the case that one is fully ordained by the very same [person] on whom one depends for ordination. 'How does one take refuge?' — he says: 'as preceptor' (<s>upādhyāyatayā</s>). 'For what purpose does one take refuge?' — he says: 'therein' (<s>tatra</s>), which refers to ordination and full ordination. And this is a locative of purpose (<s>nimittasaptamī</s>). For the purpose of ordination and full ordination, having taken refuge with a certain <s>bhikṣu</s> as preceptor, ordination and full ordination come about — not as in the former epoch, without taking refuge with anyone. Now, 'ordination' here: that which constitutes the ascetic practice therein is the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice) precepts; [the stages] connected with that should be understood. Both ordination and the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> precepts [require] one who has taken refuge. The distinction here, however, is that ordination [comes] from the preceptor himself, while the precepts [may come] from another. Regarding the method of accepting refuge for one who has taken refuge, he says — (4) Having asked about the obstructive conditions (<s>āntarāyika</s>), for the one who is pure, [the preceptor] should first grant permission for the preceptorship. What is intended here as 'obstructive' (<s>āntarāyika</s>) is that which creates obstacles to ordination, such as matricide (<s>mātṛvadha</s>) and so forth. 'Himself' (<s>svayam</s>) — here, unlike in the case of tonsure and so forth, the meaning is not that he [the candidate] should do this himself; rather, the meaning is that the [preceptor] himself should do this. 'Him' (<s>enam</s>) refers to the one to be fully ordained. When available, [the preceptor] should have [him] formally designate (<s>adhiṣṭhāpayet</s>) a [robe that has been] cut and sewn; when not available, another [garment] — this is the procedure to be followed regarding robe-material. Because the designation is for the purpose of [proper monastic] attire, it should be understood that the wearing of these [robes] follows immediately after the designation. (41) 'And having shown the bowl (<s>pātra</s>) to the <s>saṃgha</s>: [asking whether it is] proper, excessive, or too light-colored.' 'Having shown' — its connection is with 'to the <s>saṃgha</s>.' For what purpose is the showing? — He says: 'proper, excessive, or too light-colored' — for the purpose of avoiding these faults; the designation of one of this [faulty] sort would be improper. 'Having shown to the <s>saṃgha</s>, [the preceptor] should have [him] designate [it]' — this continues [from the previous sūtra]. (42) '"It is a proper bowl" — if it is not of that [faulty] sort, all should say.' 'All' means the <s>bhikṣus</s> as assembled. 'Being of that sort' (<s>evaṃbhāva</s>) means 'that-ness' (<s>evaṃtva</s>); it means being endowed with faults such as being deficient in [size], etc. 'Not being of that sort' (<s>anaivamtva</s>) means being free from those faults — this is the meaning. (43) 'Having removed [the candidate], having announced "who [shall be the private instructor]?" and having encouraged the private instructor (<s>rahonuśāsaka</s>), the <s>saṃgha</s> as act-performer should authorize him.' 'Having removed' means when the one to be fully ordained has been taken elsewhere from the consecrated area (<s>maṇḍalaka</s>); the purpose of removal here is so that the proceedings regarding the private instructor are not heard [by the candidate] — no other [reason] is apparent. Therefore, [he should be taken] to where the hearing of this [proceeding] does not reach him — this should be understood from the procedural rule. It will be stated later: 'They should place him at a distance for visual inspection, facing the assembly, with palms joined.' 'Having announced "who"' means: by the formula 'The one designated by such-and-such name as private instructor by such-and-such name' — having announced 'I am named so-and-so,' [one announces] the private instructor. 'Having encouraged' means: 'You yourself are the private instructor; do you undertake it?' — and so forth. 'Him' refers to the private instructor. 'Should authorize' — for this purpose the act-performer should make a motion (<s>jñapti</s>). Some read in the relevant formula: 'May the <s>saṃgha</s> approve so-and-so as private instructor' — that is improper, because the necessity of performing a <s>karmavācanā</s> (formal proclamation) would also follow, and there is no cause for it. This is not an approval (<s>saṃmati</s>); it is an authorization (<s>anujñapana</s>) — this is the determination. Therefore, that [formula reads]: 'May so-and-so as private instructor privately instruct so-and-so' — herein the authorization is proper; that authorization is formulated thus, not as an approval. (44) '"Listen, you" — [the private instructor] should privately instruct [the candidate].' 'Private instructor' (<s>rahonuśāsaka</s>) should be understood by implication. 'Listen, you, venerable one, this is your time for truth' — and so forth: by the words 'listen, you,' the formula is indicated by [its opening] word. 'Wait; do not [come]. When called, you shall come' — having said this to him, the private instruction is complete. (45) 'When privately instructed, [the private instructor] should announce the purity to the <s>saṃgha</s>.' This is the procedure. [By the formula:] 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear! This one has been privately instructed by me, named so-and-so' — and so forth. 'Should he come?' — [the private instructor] should ask about his coming. Thus [decides] the <s>saṃgha</s>. (46) '"He is pure" — all should say.' 'All' means the <s>bhikṣus</s> performing the full ordination. Some here and in the earlier [passage] regarding the announcement formula for ordination read that the response should be [said by]: 'The entire <s>saṃgha</s> should say: "He is pure." He should say: "Pure."' — that is unfitting. The burden of [confirming this] falls on the speaker [i.e., the private instructor], since it has already been announced first by the private instructor. (47) 'The act-performer should have [the candidate] request the <s>upasaṃpad</s> (full ordination).' [The candidate is] one who seeks full ordination. (48) 'Having obtained authorization from the <s>saṃgha</s>, [the act-performer] should ask about the obstructive conditions (<s>āntarāyika</s>).' Having made a motion (<s>jñapti</s>) for the purpose of questioning about obstructive conditions,
[VinSū 12]

children.text: ) śruṇu tvaṃ āyuṣman, ayaṃ te satyakālaḥ, ayaṃ te bnūtakāla ityādinā mantreṇa āntarāyikaparipraśnaḥ // (49) upasaṃpadamupanayet // jñapticaturthena karmaṇā // [avasarārtha karma]kārakaḥ // (50) chāyāṃ vedayeta anantaraṃ mitāmiti / upasaṃpadupanayanāntaraṃ chāyāmupasaṃpannāya vedayetetyarthaḥ / anantaraṃ avilambitam / kathaṃ vedayeta ityāha - mitāṃ saśeṣakāryasya āsanabhaṅgāyogāt karmakārakādanyena asya mānasya yogaḥ / tatpunaḥ mānamasya padādīnāṃ kena ityāha - (51) śaṃkunāṃ catura [ṅgulena eta] tsādhu // etaditi mānaṃ ciratvābhāvāya caturaṅgulena mānaṃ śobhanam // (52) puruṣatvena asyānuvyavahāraḥ // sādhu iti vartate / asyeti caturaṅgulasya śaṃkoḥ, yāvantaḥ śaṅkavaḥ tāvat pauruṣīcchāyā vaktavyā ityarthaḥ // (53) ahorātrāṃśaṃ pūrvāhaṇādikaṃ / vedayeta ityanuvartate / pūrvāhaṇo madhyāhan ityādi granthottam // (54) samayaṃ ca [pañcaite // vedaye]ta / pañcaite iti samayāḥ (55) haimantiko, griṣmiko, vārṣiko, mitavārṣiko, dīrghavārṣikaḥ iti // parimāṇameṣāmucyate - (56) cāturmāsikau pūrvau / haimantiko grīṣmikaśca // (57) māsaṃ paraṃ / iti vārṣikaḥ // (58) tato ahorātrah iti / tato vārṣikātparo mitavārṣikaḥ eko ahorātraḥ // (59) tadūnaṃ antyo māsatrayam iti / tenai kena ahorātreṇa ūnaṃ māsatrayaṃ, antyaḥ samayo dīrghavārṣikaḥ // samayavedanāntaraṃ upasaṃpannamātrāya karmakārako - (60) niḥśrayānārocayet //
children.translated_text: [by the formula:] 'Listen, you, venerable one, this is your time for truth, this is your time for reality' — and so forth: by this formula, the questioning about obstructive conditions [is performed]. (49) '[The <s>saṃgha</s>] should confer the full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>).' By a formal act with a motion and three proclamations (<s>jñapticaturtha karma</s>). The act-performer [does this] for the purpose of opportunity. (50) '[The act-performer] should announce the shadow, measured, immediately afterward.' After conferring the full ordination, [the act-performer] should announce the shadow to the newly ordained one — this is the meaning. 'Immediately afterward' means without delay. How should he announce [it]? — He says: 'measured' — for one who still has remaining duties, since it is improper to break [from the proceedings to measure] the seat, the measurement should be done by someone other than the act-performer. By what should that measurement of the steps, etc. be made? — He says: (51) 'By a peg of four finger-widths (<s>aṅgula</s>) — this is proper.' 'This' refers to the measurement; a measurement of four finger-widths is proper for the purpose of not taking too long. (52) 'Its reckoning should be in terms of a person's [height].' 'Proper' continues [from the previous sūtra]. 'Its' refers to the four-finger-width peg; as many pegs [as fit], so many [units of] a person's shadow should be stated — this is the meaning. (53) 'The portion of the day-and-night: forenoon and so forth.' 'Should announce' continues. Forenoon, midday, and so forth are elaborated in the text. (54) 'And the season — these are five.' 'Should announce' [continues]. 'These five' are the seasons: (55) the winter season (<s>haimantika</s>), the summer season (<s>grīṣmika</s>), the rains season (<s>vārṣika</s>), the short-rains season (<s>mitavārṣika</s>), and the long-rains season (<s>dīrghavārṣika</s>). Their durations are stated: (56) 'The first two are of four months.' The winter and summer [seasons]. (57) 'The next is one month.' That is the rains season (<s>vārṣika</s>). (58) 'After that, one day-and-night.' After the rains season, the next [season], the short-rains (<s>mitavārṣika</s>), is one day-and-night. (59) 'Less than that by the last: three months.' Less by that one day-and-night [equals] three months; the last season is the long-rains (<s>dīrghavārṣika</s>). After announcing the season, the act-performer [says] to the newly ordained one: (60) '[The act-performer] should announce the supports (<s>niśraya</s>).'

body.text: pāṃsukūlādayaste catvāraḥ // (61) patanīyān dharmān / pārājikān // (62) śramaṇakārakāṃśca / ākruṣṭenana pratyākroṣṭavyamityādikān ārocayediti vartate // (63) saṃpannatāṃ samyaktayā ca prepsitasya udgrāhya śīlasāmānyagatatā 'rāgaṇe niyuñjīta // prakarṣeṇepsitaṃ prepsitaṃ abhipretam / yaste bhūtapūrva āśāsakaḥ 'kaccidahaṃ labheya' ityādi idamasyābhilaṣitam / tasya saṃpannatāmudgrāhya sattvaṃ,etarhi pravrajita-upasampannetyādinā / samyaktā punaḥ sampannatāyāḥ pratirūpeṇopādhyāyena ityādinā abhihitā / saṃpannatāmudgrāhya kiṃ karttavyam ityāha - śīla sāmānya gatatā-ārāgaṇe niyuñjīta // yatra varṣaśatopasaṃpannena ityādinā śīlena sāmānyagatatā śīlasāmānyagatatā / tasyā ārāgaṇaṃ ārādhanam // (64) pātrikasaṃbandha-pratibimbane niyuñjīta / iti sarvatra adhikṛtaṃ veditavyam // pātrikasaṃbandho mātāpitṛsambandhaḥ, tasya pratibimbanaṃ - adyāgreṇa te upādhyāyasya mātṛpitṛ-saṃjñetyādinā / evaṃ te so 'bhyasto gṛhisaṃbaṃdhaḥ pratibimbayitavyaḥ iti // (65) vinīta-saṃvāsatāyām / adyāgreṇa te sagauraveṇa ityādinā // (66) prayojanānuṣṭhāne // adyāgreṇa te uddeṣṭavyamityādinā / (67) saṃpatyasyamānatāṃ asamākhyātāṃ samāttaparijñānasya ācakṣīta // imāni ca imāni te mayā audārikaudārikau [itye]vamādinā, saṃprati anākhyātasya samāttasya vṛttasya (

children.translated_text: [VinSū 13]

children.text: ) parijñāmeva saṃpatsyate iti // (68) ādare niyuñjīta // 'eṣatvamupasaṃpanna' iti gāthābhyāṃ 'prāstadikasya' iti anayā kṣaṇasampado daurlabhyaṃ darśayati, yasmāt asatsvapi anyeṣu akṣaṇeṣu, labdhe 'pi prāpye 'nukampakaiḥ dṛṣṭi saṃpanne ca manuṣyatve bahavo 'tra apariśuddhisaṃkhyā antarāyā [vairū]pyaṃ ca / tasmāt durlabhā eṣā // (69) sopāyākhyānaṃ ca saṃpādane // sahopāyākhyānena sopāyākhyānam, yadarthaṃ pravrajyopasaṃpat tatsaṃpādane niyuñjīta - upasaṃpannastvaṃ āyuṣman apramādena saṃpādaya ityanena / tadyathā anuprāptastvaṃ etatsthānaṃ, abhiratiridānīmatra kartavyā iti / sāmīcyām ādau triḥkaraṇaṃ saṃghasaṃghaṭitāyāṃ anuśiṣṭau ca niṣa[ṇṇasyo]tkuṭukikayā purataḥ iṣṭake pārṣṇibhyāṃ rahonuśiṣṭau upasaṃpadi sthitasya pātraṃ vāme pāṇau pratiṣthāpya, praticchādya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā ityādeḥ karmavastuni vakṣyamāṇatvāt iha anupanibandhaḥ // upasaṃpad vidhiḥ //
children.translated_text: ...full comprehension itself will be accomplished. (68) One should exhort [the newly ordained] to earnestness. Through the two verses beginning with 'You are now fully ordained' and with 'of the one for whom this is the starting point,' he shows the rarity of the opportune conjunction (<s>kṣaṇasaṃpad</s>), because even when other inopportune conditions are absent, even when human birth is obtained with the attainment of right views and with compassionate teachers, there are many obstacles that prevent purity, and disfigurement. Therefore this [opportunity] is rare. (69) And the explanation of the method for accomplishment. 'Together with the explanation of the method' (<s>sopāyākhyāna</s>) means: one should exhort to the accomplishment of that for whose sake the ordination was undertaken — with the words 'You are now fully ordained, Venerable One; accomplish [your purpose] with earnestness.' That is: 'You have attained this station; now delight is to be cultivated here.' As for the proper procedure — the triple performance at the beginning, the instruction assembled by the <s>saṅgha</s>, and for the privately instructed one, the placement of the bowl in the left hand while standing at ordination, covered with the right hand, etc. — since this will be stated in the <s>Karmavastu</s> (Chapter on Procedures), it is not elaborated here. // The ordination procedure //

body.translated_text: The rag-robe (<s>pāṃsukūla</s>) and the rest — those are the four [supports]. (61) 'The offenses entailing expulsion (<s>patanīya dharmas</s>)' — the <s>pārājika</s> offenses. (62) 'And the qualities that make one a true ascetic (<s>śramaṇakāraka</s>)' — such as 'when reviled, one should not revile in return' and so forth. '[The act-performer] should announce' continues [from the previous sūtra]. (63) 'Having ascertained the fulfillment and the correctness of what was desired, [the preceptor] should engage [the newly ordained] in striving for equality in moral conduct with the community.' That which is intensely desired (<s>prepsita</s>) is the intended [goal]; what he formerly wished for — 'Might I obtain [ordination]?' and so forth — this is what he aspired to. Having ascertained the fulfillment of that — the fact [of its accomplishment], through [words such as] 'Now you are ordained and fully ordained' and so forth. The correctness, moreover, of that fulfillment is expressed by [words such as] 'by a proper preceptor' and so forth. Having ascertained the fulfillment, what should be done? — He says: '[The preceptor] should engage [him] in striving for equality in moral conduct with the community.' Where [it is said] 'by one ordained a hundred years' and so forth — equality in moral conduct with the community through [such] moral conduct is 'equality in moral conduct with the community' (<s>śīlasāmānyagatatā</s>). The striving for that is its accomplishment (<s>ārādhana</s>). (64) '[The preceptor] should engage [him] in the reflection upon the [preceptor's] parental-like relationship.' This should be understood as the governing [instruction] everywhere. 'Parental-like relationship' (<s>pātrikasaṃbandha</s>) is the relationship [analogous to that] of mother and father; its reflection (<s>pratibimbana</s>) is [expressed] through [words such as] 'From this day forward, you should regard the preceptor as mother and father' and so forth. Thus that habitual household relationship of his should be reflected [onto the monastic relationship]. (65) '[The preceptor should engage him] in the conduct of disciplined communal living (<s>vinītasaṃvāsatā</s>)' — through [words such as] 'From this day forward, with reverence, you...' and so forth. (66) '[The preceptor should engage him] in the performance of duties (<s>prayojanānuṣṭhāna</s>)' — through [words such as] 'From this day forward, you should recite...' and so forth. (67) '[The preceptor] should inform [him] of the present [rules] that have not been announced, [pertaining to] the knowledge of what has been undertaken.' Through [words such as] 'These and these are the gross offenses for you' — and so forth: of what has now not been announced, of the undertaken practice that has been performed,
(iii) Matters relating to dependence (<s>niśraya</s>)

body.text: (70) nānavalokya niśrayam niśritakaraṇīyaṃ kuryāt // apṛcchanaṃ anavalokanam, apṛṣtvā na kiñcitkuryādityarthaḥ // karaṇīyeṣu avalokanaprasaktasya kiṃcitkaraṇīyasya apṛṣtvā 'pi karaṇamuktaṃ bhagavatā, ityāha - (71) muktvā uccāraprasrāvaṃ dantakāṣṭhavisarjanaṃ sopavicāravihāracaityābhivandanam // yad antarvyāpārasaṃkhyena kaṇḍanādinā vyāpāreṇa abhivyāpyate taccaityāṅganam, so 'tropavicāro yujyate / saha upavicāreṇa sopavicāraḥ, tatra caityaṃ, tasyābhivaṃdanam // (72) ekānnapañcāśat-vyāmaparyantādvihārato gamanam // muktvā ityanubandhaḥ / ekānna[pañcāśat] iti 'āṭa'-sandhiḥ ekānnapañcāśat-vyāmasya paryantādyāvat ityarthaḥ // yatra vihāre khātako vā prākāro vā anyo vā parivāro vidyate, tatra sa vihārānta iti adhyavasānaṃ yujyate / anekaprākārādi-sadbhāve sarvabāhyaḥ / tasmāt tatra tasya bāhyapārśvamasya pramāṇasyāvadhiḥ / yastu[nopa]-vicāraḥ tatra vihārabhittirevāvadhiḥ / yadatra parataḥ pūrvoktasyopavicārasya sthānaṃ, na tadgataṃ caityaṃ abhivanditavyam, ityatropatiṣṭhate // parisarpaṇabhūtasya etadanujñānam // anyacca, ataḥ caityābhivandanamiti tatra kiṃ pratipattavyam? - tadartha na gantavyam anāpṛṣṭvā / parisarpaṇārthaṃ tu gatena vanditavyamiti // dvividhametatkaraṇīyam - [ārambha]-bhūtaṃ abhinamanabhūtaṃ ca / tatra yadārambhabhūtaṃ tasyaiva pratiṣedhaḥ, abhinamanabhūtasya tu apratiṣedhyatvaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate // nānāpṛcchya ālapitavyaṃ, na saṃlapitavyaṃ, na pratisaṃmoditavyaṃ, na prativacanaṃ dātavyaṃ, nodakadigdhena pāṇinā dharmitena pādau vā mukhaṃ vā hṛdayādikaṃ vā anuparimārṣṭavyaṃ, nodakena hastādeḥ [parimārjanaṃ(?) rajovakīrṇa]-vasrādi prasphoṭayitavyaṃ ityādeḥ iti hāsapadabhūtasya vṛttasya āpatteḥ // (

) upānaha-dantakāṣṭha-pāṭhaḥ svādhyāyopasaṃhārāṇāṃ karaṇapratīṣṭoḥ tajjātīyasya bhikṣorantikāditi viśeṣaparigrahāt abhipretamatra abhinamanabhūtaṃ iti gamyate / duṣṭo 'tra pravrajito jñātaḥ śaṃkito vā anāpṛṣṭo [aparityakta]vyo(?), nānyaḥ / na hi paṭhati, svādhyāyaṃ vā kurvati, upasaṃhārasya tadanurūpe kāle karaṇaṃ ityādeḥ karaṇayītvena prajñānam / abhinamanaprakāratvena hyetasya manasi nilayanam / duṣṭe tu vipakṣānugatitvena etatpratibhāṣāmāṇaṃ ārambhatvena khyātimupagacchati / tasmāt yatra yatnaḥ kartavya ityatrābhiprāyo dṛśyate // udakapānasya anāpṛcchākaraṇaṃ anena pravicāreṇa kṛtaṃ veditavyam
// tadvidhaṃ hyetad yadvidhaṃ dharmitasya gātrāṇāmudakena saṃsparśanam // niśritavṛttaṃ ucyate - (73) pātracīvarakarmaṇi, glānopasthāne, kaukṛtyaprativinodane, pāpakadṛṣṭigatapratiniḥsarge tīvraṃ autsukyamāpadyeta - aho bata ahaṃ kuryām kārayeyaṃ vā iti // raṅgakarma api atra kecit paṭhanti / tasya cīvarakarmaṇo nātirekāt grahaṇam // (74) saṃghe praṇidhātukāme - utkṣepaṇīyādi-praṇidhikarma kartukāme saṃghe aho bata saṃgho niśrayasyedaṃ praṇidhikarma na kuryāt // iti tīvramautsukyamāpadyate, nivartate - yāvat āvṛhet iti sarvatraitadanuṣaktaṃ veditavyam // (75) kṛte avasārayet // iti praṇidhikarmaṇi kṛte - aho bata saṃgho 'sya avasārayet iti // (76) parivā[sa]-mūlaparivāsamānāpya-mūlamānāpya-ābarhaṇārthini niśraye aho bata saṃgho asya aprivāsādicatuṣkaṃ dadyāt, ābarhaṇārthini aho bata ābṛhet iti // (77) so 'pyetadasmai kuryāt, utsṛjyāvalokanam // so 'pi niśrayaḥ / etad pātracīvarakarmādi / asmai niśritāya kuryāt / utsṛjyāvalokanaṃ avalokanamekaṃ muktvā // (78) nonadaśava[rṣaḥ upasaṃpadaḥ u]pādhyāyatva-niḥśrayatva-aniśritavāsān kuryāt // upasaṃpadāya ūnadaśavarṣaḥ sa etat trayaṃ na kuryāt // (79) anūna-daśavarṣo 'pi upasaṃpadā, nāsamanvitiḥ kenacidanantarebhyaḥ samāyogena // ye 'nantaraṃ vakṣyamāṇāḥ pañcāṅgikāḥ samāyogāḥ tebhyaḥ yena kenacit ekenā 'pi samanvito yogyo[nā 'nya i]ti bhāvaḥ / evañca yaduktaṃ aparairapi pañcabhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatena ityatra na samuccayo vijñātavyaḥ ebhiḥ imaiśca aparairiti / api tu ebhiḥ tāvatkartavyaṃ ityuktam, imairapi aparaiḥ iti vikalpaḥ // kuta etad? / asaṃbhavāt sarvāsāmāsāṃ pañcikānāṃ sākṣyasya // ādyāyāṃ tu pañcikāyāṃ daśavarṣa[tvāṅga] ukte daśavarṣo bhavatyupasaṃpadeti / tadebhiḥ daśavarṣagrahaṇaṃ ādau sarvasya uttarasya eṣa viṣayaparigraha iti khyāpanārtham / sthitārthatvaṃ vinaye, daśavarṣatve sati upādhyākaraṇādau kāraṇaṃ / viśeṣabhūtatvaṃ śeṣasya tatrā 'sti cet saviśeṣatvaṃ uttamakalpaḥ / na cet etanmātrakamapi atrāvalambi[tavyam / yathā] śaikṣatvādeḥ viśeṣasya laṅghyatvam evamasyāpi daśavarṣatve sati vinaye sthitārthatvasyeti / te idānīṃ samāyogāṃ (
children.translated_text: The reading of 'sandals' and 'tooth-stick,' the reading of 'self-study' and 'conclusion' — since these are understood as being of the category 'paying of respect' from the specification 'from a <s>bhikṣu</s> of the same type in the practice of carrying out and receiving,' this is understood as intended here. A corrupted or suspected ordained person, even without being asked, is not to be abandoned — not any other. For the acts of reading, performing self-study, and concluding at the appropriate time are known as duties. This [type of behavior] rests in the mind as being of the nature of paying respect. But in the case of a corrupted person, since it follows the opponent's course, opposing it becomes known as an initiative. Therefore the intention is that effort should be made in this regard. The non-asking regarding drinking of water should be understood through this analysis, for it is of the same kind as the touching of the limbs of an anointed body with water. The dependent's duties are stated: (73) Regarding bowl-and-robe work, attendance upon the sick, removal of remorse, and abandonment of wrongly-held views — one should feel intense eagerness, thinking 'Oh, may I do this or have it done!' Some also read 'dyeing work' here; since it does not differ from robe-work, it is included. (74) When the <s>saṅgha</s> wishes to impose a formal act — when the <s>saṅgha</s> wishes to carry out a formal act of suspension etc., [one should think:] 'Oh, may the <s>saṅgha</s> not impose this formal act upon my shelter-giver!' Thus one feels intense eagerness; one desists — up to 'one should expel.' This should be understood as connected throughout. (75) When it is done, one should restore. When the formal act has been carried out — 'Oh, may the <s>saṅgha</s> restore him.' (76) For one seeking probation, original probation, <s>mānāpya</s> (penance), original <s>mānāpya</s>, or rehabilitation — regarding the shelter-giver: 'Oh, may the <s>saṅgha</s> give the fourfold [procedure] beginning with probation; for one seeking rehabilitation: Oh, may [the <s>saṅgha</s>] rehabilitate [him].' (77) He too should do this for him, setting aside consultation. 'He' refers to the shelter-giver. 'This' refers to bowl-and-robe work etc. 'For him' — for the dependent. 'Setting aside consultation' — except for consultation alone. (78) One who has not completed ten years since full ordination should not serve as a preceptor, as a shelter-giver, or dwell without dependence. One who has less than ten years since ordination should not perform these three. (79) Even one with ten or more years since ordination [should not serve as preceptor] if not endowed with any one of the following qualifications. Those five qualifications to be stated next — one who is not endowed with even one of them is not suitable; this is the meaning. And thus what is stated by others, 'endowed with five other qualities,' should not be understood as a cumulation — 'these and those others.' Rather, 'with these it should be done' is stated [first]; 'with these others also' is an alternative. How is this known? Because of the impossibility of witnessing all these sets of five. In the first set of five, since the qualification of ten years is stated, 'one becomes [eligible] for ordination at ten years'; therefore the mention of ten years at the beginning serves to indicate that this is the domain for everything that follows. When settled in purpose in the Vinaya and having ten years, there is a basis for preceptor-hood etc. The special character of the remaining [qualifications]: if present, there is superiority — the best case. If not, even this minimum should be relied upon. Just as the special [quality] of being a learner etc. can be dispensed with, so too when there are ten years and being settled in purpose in the Vinaya. Now these qualifications —
VinSū 15

) are stated: (80) Competence in the performance and causation of: attending the sick (<s>glānopasthāna</s>), removing remorse (<s>kaukṛtyaprativinodana</s>), purging wrong views (<s>pāpakadṛṣṭigatapratiniḥsarga</s>), and averting dissatisfaction and despondency (<s>anabhiratisthānapramīlana</s>). By the inclusion of competence in removing remorse, the establishment of [being grounded in the <s>Vinaya</s>] is indicated. By the inclusion of purging wrong views, [the establishment of] skill in abiding in the <s>Dharma</s>. By the inclusion of averting dissatisfaction and despondency, [the establishment of] not being separated [from the community], or of having authoritative speech. Here, by the inclusion of 'causation,' it should not be thought that even one who is incapable has performed the action. Rather, when there is understanding dependent on the trainee, what is included is the competence to engage in the activity of setting others in motion. And thus here there is the non-transgression of the inviolable cause — being grounded in the <s>Vinaya</s>. (81) Before trainee-status (<s>śaikṣatva</s>), in the non-fivefold [group]: together with morality (<s>śīlavattā</s>) and extensive learning (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>). 'Trainee-status' and 'non-trainee-status' — prior to these, the fivefold group that is stated together does not apply — namely, the endowments other than those of faith, morality, and so forth; that should be understood as accompanied by morality and extensive learning as well. Together with morality and extensive learning, morality and extensive learning form the fivefold [group]. 'Morality' here is distinguished [as] the very disqualification for communal living with one of bad morals — such that they think 'this one is virtuous' — that should be understood as his [morality]. 'Extensive learning,' moreover — in whatever endowment there is mastery of the baskets (<s>piṭakas</s>), there [one might expect] expertise in opposing doctrines of other schools, in components such as topics, words, and sentences, in prosody and poetics, or in historical narratives; but where that [expertise] does not exist, there mastery of the baskets alone should be understood. (82) Expertise in the baskets (<s>piṭakābhijñatva</s>). Expertise in <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Abhidharma), together with morality and extensive learning, constitutes the fivefold [group]. In the <s>Vinaya</s> it is stated: 'a bearer of the <s>Sūtras</s>, a bearer of the <s>Vinaya</s>, a bearer of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>; one proficient in the <s>Sūtras</s>, proficient in the <s>Vinaya</s>, proficient in the <s>Mātṛkā</s>; one skilled in the <s>Sūtras</s>, skilled in the <s>Vinaya</s>, skilled in the <s>Mātṛkā</s>; one expert in the <s>Sūtras</s>, expert in the <s>Vinaya</s>, expert in the <s>Mātṛkā</s>.' Therein, the non-forgetting of what has been learned is the 'bearing' of the <s>Sūtras</s> etc., and this applies to all three baskets. What is placed in one [basket], being seen in another — this is its state of intermixture. The capacity for discriminating separation of what is thus intermixed — this is 'skill' (<s>kauśala</s>). The application of the <s>Sūtras</s> etc. through reasoning and scripture — this is 'expertise' (<s>kovidatva</s>). The capacity to make others understand what has been thus applied — this is 'proficiency' (<s>vyaktatva</s>). All of this, together with non-forgetting, is 'expertise' (<s>abhijñatva</s>) — thus stated by the general term 'expertise.' (83) Counterbalancing these by mastery. One who is not without expertise in the baskets is capable of mastering them. Therefore, this statement of 'expertise in the baskets' should be understood as [referring to] a special [qualification]. (84) Training (<s>śikṣattā</s>) in the higher morality (<s>adhiśīla</s>), higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>), and higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>). 'Training' (<s>śikṣattā</s>) is the state of one who trains; the compound is to be treated as a <s>dvandva</s> with unity. By 'higher morality' is meant the comprehension of all <s>Vinaya</s> conduct. By 'higher mind,' [the comprehension of] the meditative absorptions (<s>dhyānas</s>). By 'higher wisdom,' the practice of seeing the truths. (85) Or, the capacity for training. The word 'or' is used for the purpose of generating confidence [in the interpretation], not for presenting an alternative. One who has not [already] trained is not capable of training in the higher morality etc. This statement of 'training' should be understood as referring specifically to a special [qualification]. (86) Thus, the code of conduct (<s>adhyācāra</s>) and the disciplinary rules constitute the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. The word 'thus' refers to the [previous aphorisms] 'training' and 'or, capacity for training' —
<s>Vinayasūtra</s> 16

children.translated_text: ) — reference [to the preceding]. And from these, two endowments arise. Therein, 'code of conduct' (<s>adhyācāra</s>) [refers to] the conventional rules (<s>samudācārika</s>). 'Discipline' (<s>vinaya</s>) [refers to] the remainder. The <s>Prātimokṣa</s> training rules and the procedural regulations, together with their accessories, constitute the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> — that which is so named. Therein are included the training rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>). (87) Being endowed with faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), learning (<s>śruta</s>), generosity (<s>tyāga</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). By 'morality' here, the comprehension of the <s>Vinaya</s> is meant. (88) With morality (<s>śīla</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), liberation (<s>vimukti</s>), and the knowledge-and-vision thereof (<s>tajjñānadarśana</s>). 'Being endowed' is the continuation [of the predicate]. By 'endowed with morality,' the implication of the <s>Vinaya</s> terminology is drawn here, not otherwise, because a <s>bhikṣu's</s> moral endowment is [only] possible [through the <s>Vinaya</s>]. In 'knowledge thereof,' the pronoun 'that' refers to liberation — thus 'the knowledge-and-vision of liberation.' (89) And being of aroused vigor (<s>ārabdhavīrya</s>) and wise (<s>prājña</s>). By the word 'and' from [the earlier aphorism] 'Before trainee-status, together with morality and extensive learning,' [additional qualities] are brought in. From here onward, [the qualities that were stated as] the non-fivefold group before trainee-status should be understood as stated together with being of aroused vigor and wise. And together with morality and extensive learning, three single [qualities] are stated here: (90-92) Mindfulness (<s>smṛtimat</s>). Seclusion (<s>pratisaṃlīna</s>). Concentration (<s>samāhita</s>). The completion of these into a set of four — one is moral, learned, of aroused vigor, wise, and mindful. Having stated this set of four again, 'and one is secluded' should be declared. Again, 'concentrated.' (93) Trainee-status (<s>śaikṣatva</s>). One is endowed with the trainee's aggregate of morality (<s>śīlaskandha</s>). This is the summary of 'being endowed with the trainee's aggregates of concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge-and-vision of liberation.' (94) Non-trainee-status (<s>aśaikṣatā</s>). What conduct is specifically determined as the nature of these two [statuses], beginning with 'being endowed with the non-trainee's aggregate of morality' — therein, the knowledge of what is proper and improper is exclusively attainment-based for these two. And the knowledge of the determination of offenses [and of] the <s>Vinaya</s> procedure of the disciplined one — therein too, these two, being established in autonomy by virtue of having ten years [of seniority] and so forth, having necessarily made effort — therefore, here no transgression of the inviolable cause should be understood [as having taken place]. (95) Expertise in origination (<s>utpatti</s>), designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), re-designation (<s>anuprajñapti</s>), rejection (<s>pratikṣepa</s>), and permission (<s>abhyanujñā</s>). From this [situation], a training rule has arisen — thus 'origination' designates the occasion for the arising of the training rule. The establishment of the training rule is 'designation' (<s>prajñapti</s>). By 'designation' is meant the comprehension of 'to this extent, and when near, a gross offense is to be confessed' and so forth. 'What is rejected and what is permitted therein' is 're-designation' (<s>anuprajñapti</s>). For example: by the permission of footwear, the prohibition of the particular type of hempen sandal and so forth. And in the prohibition of eating at improper times, the permission for the sick [to eat] on a physician's advice. 'This is absolutely never to be done' — this prescribed rule is 'rejection' (<s>pratikṣepa</s>). For example: the drinking of even a blade-tip's [amount of] liquor, and sexual misconduct and the like. 'Permission' (<s>abhyanujñā</s>), however, is that whose performance or non-performance involves no fault — there is freedom of action therein. For example: 'For the purpose of refuting opponents, external treatises may be studied' and so forth. Therein, in its performance or non-performance, there is no offense or fault. And this much knowledge of what is to be done and not done should be learned regarding the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> rules. Thus that expertise in the <s>Vinaya</s>, being additional, should be understood as indicated by the fivefold [group], and by the fivefold [group] of offenses and so forth. (96) Expertise in what is obstructive (<s>āntarāyika</s>) and non-obstructive (<s>anāntarāyika</s>), and the capacity for instruction (<s>anuśāsakatva</s>) as proclaimed —

children.translated_text: This is the analysis: what is not to be done in the <s>Vinaya</s> is obstructive (<s>āntarāyika</s>), and what is to be done is non-obstructive (<s>anāntarāyika</s>); knowledge of both these is indicative of being established in the meaning of the <s>Vinaya</s>. 'Instructor' (<s>ākhyāpitā</s>) means the ability or diligence to speak and make understood the skill regarding this twofold [classification]. 'Being an admonisher' (<s>anuśāsakatva</s>) means the capacity to speak in accordance with correction when there is transgression, and when there is laziness, he becomes one who speaks in accordance with turning [the person back]—this is the meaning of the reading '<s>anuśāsaka</s>.' Some read '<s>avavadati</s>' and '<s>anuśāsti</s>' in place of these. There, '<s>anuśāsti</s>' is equivalent to 'he is an admonisher'—by this [it is explained]. '<s>Avavadati</s>' designates the instruction that is for the purpose of mental attention. Ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) is for this purpose. Therefore he is especially worthy here, or this is subsumed under 'gathering of the assembly' (<s>parṣatsaṃgraha</s>). (97) Together with the capability for taking <s>niśraya</s> (reliance) or <s>upaniśraya</s> (secondary reliance). Capability for taking means fitness for taking; together with this capability for taking, the fivefold [qualification] beginning with knowledge of obstructive [and non-obstructive matters applies]. There are two combinations: one is to be included in the fourfold [qualification] pertaining to <s>niśraya</s>, and the other—the word 'or' is for the purpose of establishing [that it pertains to] <s>upaniśraya</s>. When the <s>upādhyāya</s> (preceptor) departs elsewhere, the capability for taking <s>niśraya</s> is employed. When the <s>upādhyāya</s> or the <s>niśraya</s> [teacher] departs elsewhere with temporary intention and remains, and due to some person's influence, the capability for taking <s>upaniśraya</s> is employed. (98) Knowledge of offenses and non-offenses, of grave and light [offenses], and being versed in the extended <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. There, knowledge of offenses and non-offenses has practical application in the assignment of what is to be done and not to be done by the dependent; knowledge of grave and light [offenses applies] in the confession of gross transgressions (<s>sthūlātyaya</s>). By being versed in the extended <s>Prātimokṣa</s>, establishment in the meaning of the <s>Vinaya</s> is shown. And by the word 'extended' (<s>vistara</s>), the entire <s>Vinaya</s> is encompassed. One should not think that the term '<s>Prātimokṣa</s>-extension' does not indicate the topics (<s>vastu</s>) and minor matters (<s>kṣudraka</s>) etc. beyond the <s>Vibhaṅga</s>, because all of this constitutes the extension of the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. Everything arises from the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> as its source. From 'Moreover, a <s>bhikṣu</s> together with <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>'—[arises] the <s>Pravrajyāvastu</s>. From 'The <s>poṣadha</s>, venerable ones'—the <s>Poṣadhavastu</s>. From 'The special <s>poṣadha</s> is the <s>pravāraṇā</s>; those of incomplete years'—the <s>Vārṣikavastu</s>. Precisely because of the connection of the <s>Pravāraṇāvastu</s> with the rainy-season retreat (<s>varṣāvāsa</s>). From 'When the <s>kaṭhina</s> is removed'—the <s>Kaṭhinavastu</s>. From 'By a <s>bhikṣu</s> whose robes are finished'—the <s>Cīvaravastu</s>. From 'The robe section and the leather-medicine section'—by the very reason of their arising from that, the <s>Carmavastu</s>. From 'Whatever medicines the Blessed One has permitted for sick <s>bhikṣus</s>'—the <s>Bhaiṣajyavastu</s>. From 'Announce the consent and purity of the venerable ones who have not come; do not strive for the splitting of a complete <s>saṃgha</s>' etc.—the <s>Kauśāmbikavastu</s> and the <s>Saṃghabhedavastu</s>. And from that which indicates the procedures beginning with ordination, and also from 'therefore by him' etc.—the <s>Karmavastu</s>. 'By crossing over, that <s>bhikṣu</s> must be placed on probation by the <s>saṃgha</s>'—from such [passages], the <s>Pāṇḍulohitavastu</s>. By the unwilling procedure etc.—the <s>Parivāsavastu</s>.

children.translated_text: Since after the determination of offenses comes the confession procedure and the confession of <s>saṃghāvaśeṣa</s> [offenses], therefore [this derives from] the <s>Poṣadhasthāpanavastu</s> (topic of suspension from <s>poṣadha</s>). By 'the great monastery of the <s>bhikṣus</s>'—the <s>Śayanāsanavastu</s> (topic of lodgings). Even for the purpose of showing the force of legal proceedings, since offense and <s>poṣadha</s> determination [is established]—the <s>Adhikaraṇavastu</s> (topic of legal proceedings). That which constitutes a component of speech, the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> with its twofold [nature] as 'conduct of that kind and of another kind in moral discipline' (<s>śīlācāra</s>), and the remainder of the topics. The exposition of the <s>kṣudrakas</s> (minor rules) and the topics contained in the <s>Mātṛkā</s> etc.—this is the inquiry. The exposition of conduct, however, comprises the inquiries and the means of disciplining. The <s>Carmavastu</s> (leather topic) and others [are found] among the sections. For indeed, without this, there is no being versed in the extended <s>Prātimokṣa</s>. By the <s>Vibhaṅga</s> alone, established procedures beginning with ordination do not come about, since even in matters to be done, only this much is shown. (99) In the absence of an elder, one should take reliance (<s>niśraya</s>) on a junior. If an elder endowed with any suitable fivefold [qualification] is not available, then this is the rule: 'Venerable one, a <s>bhikṣu</s> under sixty years for full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), by whom the <s>Prātimokṣasūtra</s> has not been learned, recited, and retained in detail, or who has departed elsewhere—O <s>Upāli</s>, he must take reliance on another.' Here, even one of sixty years who is not independent (i.e., still dependent), because there is no distinction in learning—'in the absence of an elder' etc. is stated. (100) Setting aside only the formal greeting (<s>sāmīcī</s>). In this [rule], salutation is not included in the observance of moral rules; the meaning is that the junior who has taken reliance on the elder elsewhere should be allowed to dwell together [without formal greeting]. (101) One of five years [ordination], endowed with the last qualification, may travel the countryside without reliance (<s>niśraya</s>). 'Knowledge of offenses and non-offenses' etc. is the last qualification; endowed with that, one of five years, without reliance, may travel the countryside. (102) Not otherwise, even if learned in the three <s>Vedas</s> (<s>traividya</s>). Even if endowed with the five <s>dharmas</s>, even if less than five years [ordained], since one who has fallen from the path and from the <s>Vinaya</s> undergoes painful change due to the combination of five-year moral conduct—there is no one of incomplete years; this is the intention observed here. 'Even a <s>traividya</s>'—for the purpose of reliance, knowledge of what is to be done and not to be done by the dependent is twofold, and [one must be] disciplined in both. There, although this is [someone's] natural quality due to innate knowledge, and due to the manifestation of activity through knowledge of former lives, and due to the attainment arrived at through difficult practice with little guidance—knowledge of what is to be done and not to be done may be established. Thus, for the purpose of those to be disciplined, one should take reliance. Because in the painful conduct of <s>Vinaya</s>, there is the abandonment of the natural state together with the former self. The abandonment of former nature by <s>arhats</s> is heard of.
