In the closely related narrative of the <s>Vastu</s>, it is said: 'Eating in the presence of unapproved [food] is included in the prohibition. You commit a transgression by not having cleaned the mouth-impurity before eating'—this is what is taught. In the section on reliance-conduct (<s>niśrayavṛtti</s>), the statement here is: 'The co-resident (<s>sārdhaṃvihārī</s>) or pupil (<s>antevāsī</s>) should rise early, dress properly and cover himself, discard the tooth-stick, pay respects to the shrine (<s>caitya</s>) within the boundary' etc.—the purification of mouth-impurity is this discarding of the tooth-stick. Hence this <s>sūtra</s>: (423) One should discard the tooth-stick. This is proper; therefore it should be relied upon for the purpose of cleansing mouth-impurity. How should one discard it? He says: (424) Only in a concealed [place]. (425) And likewise for defecation and urination. Only in a concealed [place]. (426) Not near a tree or wall that is used [by others]. 'Near' means in the vicinity; where the public always sits, that is 'used'—one should not discard the tooth-stick etc. there. (427) Its measure is from twelve finger-breadths up to eight. 'Its' means of the tooth-stick. In the reading 'up to eight,' the conjunction here [means]: the measure is from twelve finger-breadths down to eight finger-breadths. (428) Down to four [finger-breadths] above, in the absence [of the standard size], for one with much phlegm.

children.translated_text: of the earlier measure, this is the measure of the tooth-stick for one with much phlegm. The text on this: 'Among these, the middle [is standard], but those who have much phlegm should discard a tooth-stick measuring four finger-breadths less.' (429) It is not improper to discard it in a refuse-heap, on top of a heap of sticks. 'Of discarding' means discarding of the tooth-stick, since that is the subject. (430) There is no lack of concealment at the mouth of a drain-pipe. Here, in the discarding of the tooth-stick, at the mouth of a drain-pipe, concealment is indeed achieved—this is the meaning. (431) Within arm's reach, in such a situation at this [drain-pipe mouth], it is acceptable. 'Here' means at the mouth of the drain-pipe. 'In such a situation' means one of the nature of tooth-stick discarding, such as foot-washing etc. that needs to be done. 'Within arm's reach is acceptable' means one should not discard the tooth-stick etc. beyond arm's reach—this is the meaning. (432) One should scrape one's tongue with it. 'Its' refers to [the act of] tooth-stick discarding. (433) One should prepare a tongue-scraper. (434) Of needle-material. A needle-case is made of bronze (<s>raiti</s>), copper, iron, or bell-metal—of such materials, is the meaning. (435) A split tooth-stick is permitted for this purpose. 'For this purpose' means for the purpose of tongue-scraping. (436) Mutual rubbing of these for sharpening. 'Mutual' means against each other; 'of these' means of the split tooth-stick. (437-438) One should not vigorously scrub the teeth, tongue, or ears with a sharp [instrument]. Not quickly—meaning one should scrub gently. (439) Without injuring the flesh. That is, the flesh of the teeth etc. (440) One should not clean the teeth and tongue without first washing the area smeared with mouth-impurity, or [if water is unavailable,] without covering [it] with dust. This is connected with 'cleaning the tooth-stick.' In the absence of water, without covering with dust, one should clean the teeth and tongue. 'Cleaning' for these two respectively is the tooth-stick and the split [stick]. (441) Not noisily. One should clean the aforementioned two [teeth and tongue]. (442) This is an illustration. The cleaning of teeth and tongue with noise—other [things] are also implied by this, is the meaning. What is implied by the illustration, he shows: (443) Defecation, urination, spitting, blowing the nose, vomiting, purging, and other [bodily functions] too. There is vomiting that is not [exactly] spitting, and purging that is not [exactly] defecation—such as in nasal purging and for one with diarrhea, as in the discharge of what has been drunk. Therefore, even though defecation and spitting are mentioned, vomiting and purging are [separately] included. The expression 'and other' is for the inclusion of everything beyond defecation etc. (444) Cleansing is accomplished even from this [alternative]. Even with salt-earth (<s>uṣāṭuka</s>) or cow-dung. That is, from the discarding of the tooth-stick [practice]. Accomplishment is [achieved] even with salt-earth or cow-dung: 'When a tooth-stick is unavailable, one should cleanse the mouth with cow-dung or salt-earth'—this is the text. (445) One should pay respects to the shrine (<s>caitya</s>) immediately after performing the bodily duties. After the discarding of the tooth-stick, whatever duties need to be performed—after that [one pays respects].

body.translated_text: 'That' (<s>tam</s>) refers to the prohibition beginning with 'those with hands cut off, those with feet cut off,' and so forth — one should maintain [the same] prohibition for those of such [deformities] also. This is the meaning. Those whose hair is colored like turmeric are '<s>haridrakeśa</s>' (turmeric-haired). '<s>Siṃhakeśa</s>' (lion-haired) means '<s>harikeśa</s>' (tawny-haired). Those whose hair is colored as if dyed with indigo are '<s>haritakeśa</s>' (green-haired). Those whose hair is white from birth are '<s>avadātakeśa</s>' (white-haired) — but not those with gray hair. Those whose hair is like an elephant's are '<s>nāgakeśa</s>' (elephant-haired). Those whose heads are smooth and hairless like a copper vessel are '<s>akeśaka</s>' (hairless). One whose head has three or four thick ridges by which unevenness is visible is '<s>ghāṭośiras</s>' (ridged-head). Those whose body is bloated as if crushed, due to corpulence — separately compressed — they are '<s>vipātaka</s>' (bloated ones). Those whose round eyes are excessively compressed are '<s>saṃcūrṇākṣa</s>' (squint-eyed) [= '<s>cullākṣa</s>'?]. One whose eyes are at the position of the shoulders because they have receded into the head is '<s>skandhākṣa</s>' (shoulder-eyed). One whose urinary organ — which is the 'tail' — has been cut is '<s>lāṅgūlacchinna</s>' (tail-cut). Those for whom excessive fatigue arises from even a little activity are '<s>atikilāsin</s>' (excessively fatigued); this is a designation for weakness. 'And with four skin colors' means with dark blue, yellow, red, and white [skin] (those of condemned appearance). Only those who have such particular colorations are to be rejected, not those who have colors praiseworthy like those of the gods. Thus, for those of such [deformities], ordination and the rest have been prohibited. To show that even those who have already been ordained and fully ordained [with such conditions] should not be accepted [into the community], he says: (153) One should not admit (<s>upasthāpayet</s>) one who has been ordained [but is] corrupted by birth or body. One corrupted by birth, such as a chariot-maker (<s>rathakāra</s>) and so forth, is not to be accepted. One corrupted by body — with hands cut off and so forth — by appearance or physical form,
(a) The conduct of the dependent (<s>niśritapratipad</s>)

children.translated_text: Henceforth, the conduct of the dependent (<s>niśrita</s>) is taken as the governing [topic] and should be understood [accordingly]. // (447) Immediately after this, [the dependent] should approach early in the morning and pay respects. // 'After this' means after the completion of bodily duties and <s>caitya</s> (shrine) veneration, which are fixed. The dependent should perform bodily duties when in good health; therefore, [approaching] even earlier than that should be understood as [the time for visiting] the shelter-giver (<s>niśraya</s>). Since veneration with a purified mouth should desirably come first; otherwise, it would cause disruption for the dependent. Nor should one think there is a contradiction with [the sūtra] 'offering warm water and tooth-stick,' since there is room [for both] in the case of illness and the like. // (448) Inquiring about [the shelter-giver's] welfare. // (449) Offering warm water and a tooth-stick (<s>dantakāṣṭha</s>). // (450) After inspecting the kitchen (<s>mahānasa</s>), informing [the shelter-giver]. // Regarding what drink has been prepared there — that is the informing: // (451) Mentally noting what is pleasing [to the shelter-giver] so as to offer it. // Thus, when informed, one mentally notes — 'I shall offer this [particular item] that pleases him' — this is the mental noting. // (452) Cleaning the bowl (<s>pātra</s>). // (453) If there is a determination to go on alms-round (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>), also [cleaning] the water-strainer (<s>rāvaka</s>). // Cleaning of [the vessel] also known by the second name <s>ravakṣaraka</s>; a <s>rāvaka</s> is so called because it 'makes a sound' (<s>raiti śabdaṃ karoti</s>). // (454) And also [cleaning] the water-filter (<s>parisrāvaṇa</s>), if there is a purpose. // 'Cleaning' is the connection. children.translated_text: [or for robe-mending,] there is no fault in not showing slight concern. // (475) Also [duties such as] rendering things allowable (<s>kalpikīkaraṇa</s>), procuring small greens, gathering flowers and fruits, collecting tooth-sticks, and the like, in the service of the <s>śramaṇa</s> (renunciant). // The sense naturally follows that these are duties toward the shelter-giver (<s>niśraya</s>). And 'all that was previously stated' [is included] — from the word 'also' (<s>api</s>). When there is work to be done for the <s>Saṃgha</s> as well, one should understand from the [overall] guidance that this is his duty. // (476) One should wake one who is inside by knocking on the door-bolt (<s>argaḍaka</s>). // [This applies to] the shelter-giver and other <s>bhikṣus</s>. This rule applies to all [without distinction]. // (477) This should be [done] gently. // [That is,] the knocking of the door-bolt. // (478) Not excessively repeatedly. // The meaning is: one should not knock the door-bolt again and again. Nor should one bang on it. // (479) One should not push it with excessive force. // The meaning is: one should not thrust the door-bolt — also known as the door-panel (<s>kavāṭa</s>) — with excessive force. // (480) One should enter gently, with awareness, and exit without rubbing against the door-frames. // The meaning is: in such a manner that there is no abrasion against either [frame]. // (481) One should show respect to him. // 'Him' refers to the shelter-giver. Since the topic of shelter-giver and dependent is uninterrupted in the intervening [passage], the word 'him' refers back to the shelter-giver. // (482) One should stay close [to him]. // 'To him' carries over [from above]; the meaning is: one should live in close association with the shelter-giver; one should not become distant. // (483) Not [close to] one who is opposed to that [shelter-giver]. // 'Should stay close' is the connection. The meaning is: one should not associate with one who is opposed to the shelter-giver. // (484) One should feel shame on account of him. // 'On account of him' means on account of the shelter-giver. What is stated amounts to: one should be modest before him. // (485) One should be diligent in his duties. // 'Diligent' means not lazy; 'his' means of the shelter-giver. // (486) Acting with proper respect. // Whatever is to be done for him should be done with due respect — this is the meaning. // (487) Having a pleasing deportment. // Endowed with a pleasing manner of walking and the like. // (488) Possessed of modesty (<s>hrī</s>) and respectfulness. // Although respectfulness (<s>gaurava</s>) is a particular form of modesty, nevertheless, since the meaning of this [term] does not follow from that word [alone], it is [separately] mentioned. Modesty (<s>hrī</s>) is the contraction [of one's conduct] from [improper] expansion. // (489) Having a sense of propriety (<s>sapratīśa</s>). // A particular form of shame (<s>apatrāpya</s>) that has the nature of perceiving one's dependence on others is called having a sense of propriety. // (490) Having a humble mind. // [That is,] one whose pride is struck down. // (491) Mindfully, not neglecting one's own duties. // [Such as] <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), and the like. // (492) One should be a seeker of what is wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>), or [diligent] in duties. // In this [context], the dependent should be a seeker of what is wholesome, taking guidance from the shelter-giver, asking questions, and regarding offerings of attendant-service and the like and in other matters — one should not be occupied with worldly affairs while doing these things; this is the meaning. // (493) One should restrain [the shelter-giver] when he is undergoing a change [for the worse]. // If that shelter-giver is undergoing some misconduct, the dependent should restrain him. // (494) If there is no growth in wholesomeness, one should request transfer to another who brings about such [growth]. // If for this dependent there is no growth in wholesomeness under that shelter-giver, then he should request transfer to another shelter-giver who brings about growth in wholesomeness. // And that [new shelter-giver] too, through questioning and the like — (495) Having ascertained [the candidate's worthiness], should assign [him] to one worthy of being a shelter-giver. // After that too, what the shelter-giver should do for the dependent: // (496-497-498) Restraining [the dependent] from bad companions. // Directing [him] toward what is wholesome. // Drawing [him] toward that [wholesomeness]. // The meaning is: drawing [the dependent] toward what is wholesome. // (499) In the rehabilitation from a transgression (<s>āpatti</s>), when there is conformity, and when there is a state of livelihood and requisites,

From the <s>sūtra</s> four [rules] earlier — 'He too should do this for him' — it should be understood that the dependent also should make effort for the accomplishment of these two for the shelter-giver. // (500) A co-resident (<s>sārdhavihārin</s>), pupil (<s>antevāsika</s>), preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), one with a common preceptor (<s>samānopādhyāya</s>), one with a common teacher (<s>samānācārya</s>), an <s>ālaptaka</s> (one greeted affectionately), a <s>saṃlaptaka</s> (a conversational companion), a <s>saṃstutaka</s> (an intimate associate), and a <s>sapremaka</s> (a dear friend) should attend upon the sick. // An <s>ālaptaka</s> is one who has been brought [into friendship] through affectionate conduct such as fond address. A <s>saṃstutaka</s> is one with whom, through going together to one place etc. and approaching through familiarity, an intimate bond has arisen. children.translated_text: others — this is the meaning. (543) He should take care [of them]. The departing <s>saṃgha</s>-elder — he should care for [them] by accomplishing what is to be done: the conduct of the <s>saṃgha</s>, deportment (<s>īryāpatha</s>), instruction, recitation, distribution of food, and provisions for the sick, and so forth. 'Conduct' (<s>caryā</s>) means going for alms. 'Deportment' (<s>īryā</s>) means deportment of the body. The instruction regarding these two [means]: 'this is proper alms-ground, this is improper alms-ground, one should go thus' — and so forth. In 'recitation and so forth' (<s>uddeśādi</s>), the word 'and so forth' includes study-sessions (<s>svādhyāyanika</s>) and the like. (544) One who has entered the rains-retreat, having taken note [of the condition], should have the <s>vihāra</s> repaired if it is not being repaired, and should encourage one who is repairing it. (545) Everyone should benefit those who have come to the assembly, when a talk is desired, by concluding with a <s>Dharma</s> exposition appropriate [to each]. If those who have come to the assembly desire a talk, then by whatever <s>Dharma</s> conclusion is suitable for each, [the elder] should benefit [them]. 'Everyone' means the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder — and not only the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder of the rains-retreat. (546) Those who are devoted to silence should be left undisturbed. 'Silence' (<s>tūṣṇītva</s>) is the state of being silent. 'Noble silence' (<s>āryatūṣṇībhāva</s>) is intended here, not mere wordlessness. (547) If householders come, [the elder] should share food [with them]. It is proper to give food to them. Having informed the <s>bhikṣus</s>, if those <s>bhikṣus</s>, when told by the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder, do not share, or if those householders do not wish to eat, then: (548) If they refuse or are reluctant, having made this <s>Dharma</s>-talk, he should say: 'This is what we have [to offer].' (549) Every assembly-holder should inspect the assembly. 'Everyone' means every assembly-holder — not only the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder — this is the meaning. (550) He should restrain one whose conduct is idle. 'Every assembly-holder' continues in connection. The meaning is that [the elder] should act so that [the monk] does not waste time idly and does not make his going forth purposeless. (551) Going and so forth here should be done as is appropriate. 'One should go thus, one should stand thus' and so forth — the word 'and so forth' refers to [these things] according to the arrangement [of the place]. 'Here' means in the assembly. 'As appropriate' means in accordance with the assembly, fitting to the assembly — this is the meaning. (552) One should not engage in various or idle talk. 'Here' continues. Talk that has strayed from the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, going sideways [from the topic], is idle talk (<s>tiryakkathā</s>); various talk (<s>nānākathā</s>) is [talk that is] scattered. (553-554) A junior attendant (<s>paścācchramaṇa</s>) should not walk in front [of the senior]. He should not stand [in front]. The meaning is: he should not stand in front of or behind the senior monk. (555) When spoken to, he should reply. Nothing should be said without being spoken to [first]. (556) He should accomplish [what is asked]. Whatever is said to him by the senior monk (<s>puraḥśramaṇa</s>), he should accomplish — this is the meaning. (557) He should not interrupt [the senior's] speech. When the senior monk is making a talk, he should not interject a speech in the middle — this is the meaning. (558) If [the senior] is speaking what is contrary to <s>Dharma</s> — the senior monk — [the attendant] should object. (559-560) [If the senior speaks] <s>Dharma</s>, [the attendant] should express approval. [The attendant] should accept gains that are properly obtained according to <s>Dharma</s>. Thus [ends the section on] the attendant monk. This is the conduct of the junior attendant.

body.translated_text: (538) A visiting [<s>saṃgha</s>-elder] should inspect and announce to the resident [monks] regarding lodgings. The visiting <s>saṃgha</s>-elder should inspect regarding lodgings; to those for whom he is the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder — the resident [monks] — he should announce regarding lodgings. (539) When departing, [the <s>saṃgha</s>-elder], having weighed the direction, caravan, dwelling, lodging, companions, and — in case of illness — non-companionship, should set out. The departing <s>saṃgha</s>-elder [should consider]: the instructions for those departing are inferred from context — in whichever direction one must travel, with whichever caravan and along whichever route, whichever is the dwelling, and the lodging there when one has arrived — all this should be weighed with discernment as to what is fitting and unfitting; and regarding companions, in case of illness, no one should be abandoned by anyone — having weighed thus, he should set out for the purpose of reaching the intended destination. (540) [The elder should say] to all, having gone to a certain distance before departing: 'Let nothing of anyone's be stolen afterward.' The <s>saṃgha</s>-elder himself [should do this]. (541) He should establish the juniors in being neither agitated nor arrogant. Non-tranquility is agitation (<s>auddhatya</s>); rigidity is arrogance (<s>unnaḍatva</s>) — he should establish [them] in the opposite [of these] — this is the meaning. (542) And everyone [should establish] all who have come near in what is wholesome. 'He should establish in being neither agitated nor arrogant' continues in connection. Not only the departing elder, but others too. And not only the juniors, but also
(c) The conduct of a monk visiting families (<s>kulopasaṃkrāmī-bhikṣu</s>).

children.translated_text: (564) One should engage them in giving (<s>dāna</s>), self-control (<s>dama</s>), restraint (<s>saṃyama</s>), the celibate life (<s>brahmacarya</s>), observance of <s>upoṣadha</s>, going for refuge (<s>śaraṇagamana</s>), and taking the training rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>). 'Them' refers to householders. '<s>Dama</s>' (self-control) is subjugation—the state of having the sense-faculties, body, and speech brought under control. '<s>Saṃyama</s>' (restraint) is their non-dispersal, discipline, and the state of being regulated. '<s>Brahmacaryavāsa</s>' (celibate life) means the conduct of one gone forth; for a householder, it means lifelong abstention from sexual intercourse. (565) In every undertaking that is a gateway to offenses, one should proceed with mindfulness. 'With mindfulness' means directed toward offenses—this is the understanding. In undertakings such as entering families, whatever going forth is a gateway for the arising of offenses, there mindfulness should be established such that one does not fall into anything. (566) One who is not instructed should not follow. 'Should proceed' is the continuation. This one has not been instructed [but is still] attached; therefore he should not proceed. The meaning is: he should not transgress his admonition. (567) One should be one who says 'Come!' preceded by 'Welcome!,' speaking pleasantly to one who has arrived. 'Come!'—one who speaks 'Welcome!' and who, from greeting one who has come earlier, speaks pleasantly—this is the meaning. 'To one who has arrived' means to a householder or a renunciant. (568) With an open and bright countenance—that is, without being gloomy. (569) Preceded by a smile. One who first approaches with a smile, one who gives a welcoming face—this is the meaning. Even in an intermediate undertaking there should be smiling, he says: (570) Free from frowning. (571) If a householder has arrived, one should give him a talk on the <s>Dharma</s>. (572) When [the householder] does not come, a monk near the village should, according to ability, engage in what is pleasing [to generate faith]. 'When not coming' refers to the householder. 'Near the village' refers to the <s>bhikṣu</s>. One should engage in what is pleasing, such as offering food etc., according to ability. (573) One should provide water and a seat. Even for a forest-dwelling [monk]—'water and seat' is the analysis. (574) A junior monk should perform sweeping, allocation of lodgings, providing water, serving, and distributing food. At every assembly, all of this should be done by the junior. (575) One should tolerate contrary conduct of attendants, provided it is not harmful to oneself or others. 'Should tolerate' means overlook. Provided that what is being tolerated does not become harmful to oneself or others. (576) If for him—if that conduct of the attendant is harmful—when one has the ability, having eliminated that contrary conduct, another— righteous—conduct—having produced [it], one should instruct—the attendant—accordingly. (577) In case of [the attendant's] dejection or illness, the remedy is on account of that. When that righteous conduct is being introduced, if that attendant experiences mental distress (dejection) or illness, or departure by another, the remedy [should be applied]. One should remedy it through gifts etc., so that the attendant does not experience either of these two. (578) When unable [to remedy], one should move on with another. When unable to eliminate [the problem], one should proceed with another [attendant]. (579) But one should not—having quarreled—speak—to the attendant—about that reason. (580) In a monastery (<s>saṃghārāma</s>), when one who has transgressed acts thus, he should allow himself to be arrested by the self-appointed [authority]. body.translated_text: The conduct of one who visits families is now stated. (561) [He should be] unarrogant — thus, everyone, at the household, should be unarrogant [and] unsettled. Being unsettled (<s>anavasthitatva</s>) means the desire to depart from the house. (562) With downcast eyes. With eyes restrained from sense-objects — this is the meaning. (563) He should give a <s>Dharma</s>-talk to the householders.

children.translated_text: This vow should not be observed beyond this [period]. Therefore, when this time period is complete, before full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), one should not train in this training, or this restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) is destroyed — this should be understood. What is the time for the arising of probationary status (<s>śikṣamāṇātva</s>)? [The sūtra] states: // (590) [The time] for the arising [of probationary status] begins at [the age that is] less than the ordination-age by that [training period]. // The beginning of the ordination-age — it is of two kinds for her: for an unmarried girl (<s>kumārikā</s>), twenty years of age; for one who has lived in a household (<s>gṛhoṣitā</s>), twelve years. The beginning [of probationary training] is at the ordination-age minus the training period of two years; this is the time for the arising of probationary status. For an unmarried girl, it is eighteen years; for one who has lived in a household, it is ten years — this is the meaning. // The textual passage in the <s>Bhikṣuṇīvibhaṅga</s> states: 'One who has lived in a household for ten years, or an unmarried girl of eighteen years — for her, the training-restraint (<s>śikṣā-saṃvṛti</s>) should be given for two years.' // Regarding the obstacle to the ordination-age that has been accepted here, a distinction is explained: // (591) Twelve years is the beginning [of ordination-age] in the case of a married woman. // 'Married' means one for whom a marriage has been performed, one who has been given in marriage; twelve years is the beginning of the ordination-time. // (592) The arising [of probationary status] is from the giving [of training-restraint]. // 'Of probationary status' carries over. By whom is it given? [The sūtra] states: // (593) By the <s>bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha</s> (community of nuns). // How? [The sūtra] states: // (594) The giving is [the bestowal of] the training-restraint (<s>śikṣā-saṃvṛti</s>). // This is an indication of the formal statement (<s>mantra</s>) beginning with: 'This one named such-and-such requests the training-restraint; the <s>Saṃgha</s> gives the training-restraint.' // (595) Immediately after this, the proclamation of the trainings. // Immediately after the giving of the training-restraint, the trainings should be proclaimed — six <s>dharmas</s> (rules) and six <s>anudharmas</s> (subsidiary rules). // What are the six <s>dharmas</s>?

body.translated_text: What pertains to <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> is now stated. There, what was said regarding 'a man' (<s>puruṣa</s>) in ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>)—the same applies to a woman, with the distinction being specified accordingly. (582) A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [stands] in the place of a <s>bhikṣu</s>. Where a <s>bhikṣu</s> is mentioned—whether as part of the <s>saṃgha</s>, individually, as preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), announcer (<s>ārocaka</s>), etc.—a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should be understood there. Is [this] in the place of every <s>bhikṣu</s>, or of certain ones? He says: (583) Of every [bhikṣu] in regard to ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>). In the domain of ordination, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> should be understood in the place of every <s>bhikṣu</s>—preceptor etc. The announcement for the purpose of the preceptress (<s>upādhyāyikā</s>), the giving of the <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice) vows—all of this is to be performed by <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> only. There is no jurisdiction of a <s>bhikṣu</s> here—this is what is taught. (584) In full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), in the place of another [bhikṣu] from the request onward, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [acts as] the officiant. In full ordination, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> is not to be understood in the place of every <s>bhikṣu</s>. Rather, from the request for full ordination onward, in the place of a <s>bhikṣu</s> other than the officiant, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> [should be understood]. From the request for full ordination onward, the officiant here is a <s>bhikṣu</s> only, not a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>—this is what is stated. But prior to the request for full ordination, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> is the officiant—she who, in the assembly of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> only, gives permission in the examination of celibate conduct (<s>brahmacaryopasthāna</s>). (585) Here, the <s>saṃgha</s> should be understood as assembled. Here, in full ordination, from the request onward, the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> should be understood as the assembled [body]. When both <s>saṃghas</s> have convened, from the request onward, the formal act (<s>karma</s>) should be performed—this is the meaning. (586) The questioning by the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> about whether there are obstructions (<s>āntarāyika</s>)—this questioning takes place in the assembly in two ways: one in the assembly of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> alone, and two—regarding the examination of celibate conduct and giving of permission—in the assembly of both <s>saṃghas</s>. This procedure should be followed for both. This is stated on account of modesty; therefore, for the purpose of ascertaining sexual conduct, the verbal formula is employed first. (587) The status of <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> (female probationer) is an additional stage for women. The status of <s>śrāmaṇerikā</s> (female novice) and <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun)—these two stages are shared with men. But this third stage is [unique] for her. And that [stage]: (588) Only for one who is dependent (<s>niśritā</s>). The word 'only' (<s>eva</s>) is for showing non-distinction from the status of <s>śrāmaṇerikā</s> and <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>—just as those two stages [require dependence], so does this one. Therefore, the practice is: for the <s>upādhyāyikā</s> (preceptress), [she should depend on] some <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, and not necessarily the same one as for the <s>śrāmaṇerikā</s> stage. Thus, for a woman, the preceptor has three [stages], while for a man, two—this is established. At what stage is the status of <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> an additional stage for women, and for how long is its practice? He says: (589) In the interval between <s>śrāmaṇerikā</s> status and <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> status, the period is the practice of two years. Having practiced for that length of time, full ordination is [given]—thus is the delimitation of time.

body.translated_text: She should not accept gold; she should not remove hair from the private parts;

body.text: na khanet pṛthivīṃ cā 'pi / na chindyāt haritaṃ tṛṇam //
body.translated_text: she should not dig the earth, nor should she cut green grass;
she should not eat what has not been [formally] received, nor should she eat food that has been stored;
these six subsidiary rules (<s>anudharmas</s>) have been stated, since the probationers must be trained [in them].

body.text: (596) na alabdhabrahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛteḥ upasaṃpad // upasaṃpad atra brahmacaryam, tasyopasthānaṃ upajananaṃ, brahmacaryopasthānāya saṃvṛtiḥ brahmcaryopasthānasaṃvṛtiḥ, sā na labdhā yayā sā iyaṃ alabdhabrahmacaryopasthānasaṃvṛtiḥ, tasyāḥ / upasaṃpad na bhavati, [yasmāt] upasaṃpadārthā saiṣāṃ saṃvṛtiḥ / kṣetratāyāṃ niyamanaṃ ityato asyāṃ alabdhārthā (

children.text:
) nopasaṃpad / kadā asyāḥ dānam - (597) rahonuśāsanādūrdhvaṃ taddānam // tasya brahmacaryopasthānasaṃvṛteḥ dānam // kenetyāha - // (598) saṃghena // prakṛtatvāt bhikṣuṇīsaṃghena pratipattiḥ // kiṃ evameva asyā dānamityāha - // (599) pṛṣṭvā āntarāyikam // tadevaṃ asyāḥ trayaḥ āntarāyikapraśnāḥ bhavanti / eko-rahonuśāsikayā bhikṣuṇyā, dvitīyaḥ-kevalabhikṣuṇī saṃghamadhye brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛtyaṃgabhūtaḥ, tṛtīyaḥ ubhayasaṃghe yācitāyāmupasaṃpadi upasaṃpadaṅgabhūtaḥ / yacanamatra yācite / karmādānaṃ ityataḥ prāptam, tato 'syāmapi yācitāyāmeva dānaṃ yuktarūpaṃ, ityāha - // (600) yācitāyāmiti // yācitāyāṃ brahmacaryopasthānasaṃvṛtau asyāḥ brahmacaryopasthānasaṃvṛterdānaṃ, na ayācitāyāmityarthaḥ // (601) paṃcatvaṃ cīvareṣu // bhikṣuṇyāḥ tricīvaraṃ, kusūlakaṃ saṃkakṣikā ca adhike // (602) niśrayeṣu vivṛkṣamūlatvam // vivarjitavṛkṣamūlatvaṃ, vṛkṣamūlaṃ varjayitvā anye trayo 'syāḥ niśrayāḥ // (603) aṣṭatvaṃ patanīyeṣu // 'sparśaḥ paṃjaranikṣepaḥ praticchādo nivāraṇaṃ' ityadhikāścatvāraḥ // (604) gurudharmārocanam // aṣṭau gurudharmā ārocayitavyāḥ / te punaḥ - "upasaṃpad bhikṣubhyaḥ / pratipakṣaṃ cāvavādaparyeṣṭiḥ // nā 'bhikṣuka āvāse / kutraci varṣopagamanaṃ ca // bhikṣorāpa tsucodanam / aroṣaṇaṃ vandanā ca navakasya // ubhayagaṇāt mānāpyam / pravāraṇā ceti gurudharmāḥ // " kasmin kāle tadārocanamityāha - // (605) patanīyaśramaṇakarakāntarāle // (606) kṛt-ṣaṭke // 'pūrvapravrajite' ti - ato yāvatkṛt iti asya yaḥ saṃjñāvān 'mā 'si' iti pravrajyārthamupasaṃkrāntāṃ pṛcchet upasaṃpādakāśca na pravrājayeyurupasaṃpāda[ye]yurvā iti sa pratipattavyaḥ ityarthaḥ // (607) nāsti asyāḥ prarohaṇadharmatā iti ca // etacca atra vidhiṣaṭkaṃ pratipattavyam / nāśanaṃ evaṃvidhasya liṅginaḥ ityetatsarvādhikārikatvāt vaktavyam / punariheti veditavyam / katamatṣaṭkamityāha - // (608)-(613) ubhayavyaṃjanā // saṃbhinnavyaṃjanā // sadāprasravaṇī // alohinī // naimittikī // keyaṃ naimittikī nāma ityāha - // nimittamātrabhūtavyaṃjanā tadākhyā // nimittamātrabhūtaṃ vyaṃjanaṃ yasyāḥ tasyāḥ naimittikīti ākhyā, saṃjñā // (614) pūrvapravrajitā / 'mā 'si ubhayavyaṃjanā' yāvat 'mā 'si pūrvaṃ pravrajitā' iti
pravrajyārthamupasaṃkrāntāṃ pṛcchet // yāvat 'nāsti asyāḥ prarohaṇadharmatā' ityeṣa atra nayaḥ pratipattavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: does not [receive] full ordination. When is the giving of this? — (597) The giving of that [restraint] is after the private instruction (<s>rahonuśāsana</s>). // The giving of the <s>brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛti</s>. // By whom? [The sūtra] states: // (598) By the <s>Saṃgha</s>. // Since the <s>bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha</s> (community of nuns) is the subject, the procedure [belongs to them]. // Is the giving merely like this? [The sūtra] states: // (599) Having asked the obstructive [questions]. // Thus there are three sets of obstructive questions for her: the first by the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) who gives private instruction, the second in the assembly of nuns alone as part of the <s>brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛti</s>, and the third in the assembly of both [monks and nuns] when full ordination is requested, as part of the full ordination. The requesting is when [the candidate] has been requested. From 'the undertaking of the act' this is obtained; therefore, the giving is proper only when she has requested — [the sūtra] states: // (600) When requested. // The giving of the <s>brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛti</s> to her is when she has requested it, not when she has not requested — this is the meaning. // (601) Five [is the number] regarding robes. // A <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> has the three robes (<s>tricīvara</s>), plus a bodice (<s>kusūlaka</s>) and a shoulder-cloth (<s>saṃkakṣikā</s>) as additional. // (602) Regarding supports (<s>niśrayas</s>), the tree-root is excluded. // Having excluded the tree-root [as a dwelling place], the other three are her supports. // (603) Eight [is the number] regarding offenses entailing expulsion (<s>patanīya</s>). // 'Touch, confinement in a cage, concealment, and obstruction' — these four are additional. // (604) The proclamation of the heavy rules (<s>gurudharmas</s>). // Eight <s>gurudharmas</s> are to be proclaimed. They are: 'Full ordination from the <s>bhikṣus</s>; and seeking instruction every fortnight; // not [dwelling] in a place without <s>bhikṣus</s>; and entering the rains-retreat (<s>varṣopagamana</s>) somewhere; // censuring a <s>bhikṣu</s> [is prohibited]; and not becoming angry; and the junior [nun] must pay reverence; // the <s>mānāpya</s> (penance) from both communities; and the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony) — these are the <s>gurudharmas</s>.' // At what time is their proclamation? [The sūtra] states: // (605) In the interval between [the recitation of] offenses entailing expulsion and the novice's duties (<s>śramaṇakaraka</s>). // (606) The set of six connected with 'kṛt.' // From 'previously ordained' — up to the extent of 'kṛt,' the one who is 'conscious' — 'Are you not?' — this should be asked of one who has approached for the purpose of ordination, and the ordainers should not ordain or give full ordination — this should be understood; this is the meaning. // (607) And: 'There is no nature of regrowth in her.' // This set of six rules should be applied here. 'Expulsion of such a person who bears the marks' — this is to be stated since it applies universally. It should be understood that [this applies] again here. What is the set of six? [The sūtra] states: // (608)-(613) One with both sex-characteristics (<s>ubhayavyañjanā</s>). // One with broken sex-characteristics (<s>saṃbhinnavyañjanā</s>). // One who constantly discharges (<s>sadāprasravaṇī</s>). // One with no menstruation (<s>alohinī</s>). // One who is merely nominal (<s>naimittikī</s>). // What is this <s>naimittikī</s>? [The commentary] states: // One whose sex-characteristic exists only in nominal form — her designation is <s>naimittikī</s>. // (614) One previously ordained. // 'Are you one with both characteristics?' up to 'Were you previously ordained?' — this should be asked of one who has approached for the purpose of ordination. // Up to 'there is no nature of regrowth in her' — this is the procedure to be followed here.

body.translated_text: (596) There is no full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>) for one who has not obtained the restraint of the approach to the holy life (<s>brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛti</s>). // 'Full ordination' here means the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>); its 'approach' (<s>upasthāna</s>) means its generation; the restraint for the approach to the holy life is the <s>brahmacaryopasthāna-saṃvṛti</s>; one who has not obtained it — for her, full ordination does not occur, since this restraint serves the purpose of full ordination. From [the rule that] 'there is restriction regarding the domain' — she who has not obtained the purpose in this [regard],
[This concludes] what pertains to the <s>Pravrajyāvastu</s> (Section on Ordination) in the <s>Kṣudraka</s> and other [texts].
(vi) Matters relating to questions. (a) Restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) and non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>).

body.text: (615) na amanuṣyagatikauttarakauravakayoḥ savarasya kṣetratvam // manuṣyagateḥ anyasyāṃ gatau upapannaḥ, manuṣyagatikatve 'pi auttara-kauravakaḥ [ca]; naiṣāṃ saṃvaraḥ (

children.text: ) ārohati ityarthaḥ // (616) na tṛtīyasyāṃ parivṛttau vyaṃjanasya // saṃvarasya na kṣetratvamityanubandhaḥ // yasya trir-vyaṃjanaṃ parivartate, na tasya saṃvaro rohatītyarthaḥ // (617) na prathamadvayoḥ dhvastiriti // na prathamadvitīyayoḥ vyaṃjanaparivṛtyoḥ dhvaṃsaḥ saṃvarasyetyarthaḥ / kṣudrakebhyaḥ etadvidhidvayaṃ sādṛśyād hṛṣṭam // (618) utthānaṃ gṛhyamāṇatve // samādīyamānatve vyaṃjanaparivṛttau satyāṃ utthānaṃ saṃvarasya // "upasaṃpadāpekṣiṇo vyaṃjanaṃ parivartate - upasaṃpanno vaktavyo 'nupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ // āha - anupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ // bhikṣubhyo hi bhikṣuṇyā upasaṃpadā bhikṣuṇībhāvaḥ paryeṣitavyaḥ" iti atra granthaḥ // nidarśanamatra puruṣasyavyañjanaparivṛttiḥ / nirāśaṅka-taratvāt anyatvamatra vidheḥ / upasaṃpadyamānāvastho 'tra upasaṃpatprekṣī gṛhītaḥ, prākparivṛtto bhikṣumātrasaṃnipātasya ayogāt // (619) anupādhyāyakatāyāṃ tadvataḥ // tadvataḥ iti upādhyāyavataḥ / saṃvarasya vinā 'pi upādhyāyena bhavati utthānam // (620) anupasaṃpannatve 'sya // upādhyāyasyopa saṃpannatve 'pi upādhyāyavataḥ saṃvarasya bhavatyutthānam? - // (621) na, jānāne 'sya abhikṣutvam // na utthānaṃ upādhyāyavataḥ saṃvarasya jānāne samādātari asyopādhyāyasya abhikṣutvaṃ anupasaṃpannatvaṃ dhvastatāṃ vā / grantho 'tra - 'upasaṃpadāpekṣī stainyasaṃvāsikena upādhyāyena upasaṃpādyate, upasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ, anupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ? - / āha - yadi jānīte stainyasaṃvāsiko me upādhyāyaḥ ityanupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ / yadi na jānāti, upasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ // evaṃ pūrvāpannakena upādhyāyena"........ityādi // ādivyagrakeṇāgārikeṇa upādhyāyeneti / nanu ca anupādhyāyatve 'pi saṃvarasyotthānam, tatkathaṃ jānāne asyā 'bhikṣutvaṃ na bhavati, yasmāt vipanno jānā[tī]tyāśayo bhavati, śīle 'nāhato bhavati, anartho vā śīlena ityataḥ etadutthānam [iti cet, tanna] / nājānāti anupādhyāyatāṃ yāvat, tasmāt avirodho 'tra anutthānasya // yattu upādhyāyasya anupasaṃpannatve saṃvarasya utthānamuktaṃ saṃghamadhikṛtya etad, saṃghasyānupasaṃpannatāṃ jānānena bhavati utthānaṃ, na upasaṃpatprekṣī [iti] // (622) nainaṃ pratyācakṣaṇe // saṃvaramukhatvāt upādhyāyasya tad-pratyācakṣaṇe nāsti saṃvarasya utthānam // grantho 'tra - upasaṃpadyamānaḥ upādyāyaṃ pratyākhyātaṃ upasaṃpanno vaktavyo 'nupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ? - āha - anupasaṃpanno vakta[vya] iti // (623) na anayoḥ nāma-anudbhāvane // anayoḥ kṣetropādhyāyoḥ samādātrā [karma]kārakeṇa vā nāmānutkīrtane na bhavati saṃvarasya utthānam // (624) na saṃghasya tadyoneḥ // samādātṛ-karmakārakābhyāṃ anyatareṇā 'pi saṃghasya nāmno 'nudbhāvane, tadyoneḥ, saṃghayoneḥ, tadvaṃśasya, saṃvarasya na bhavatyutthānam // grantho 'tra - "samādātāraṃ (
children.translated_text: ) ...arises — that is the meaning. // (616) Not upon the third change of sexual characteristics (<s>vyañjana</s>). // The continuation is: there is no ground for the restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). For one whose sexual characteristics change three times, the restraint does not arise — that is the meaning. // (617) There is no destruction [of the restraint] upon the first two [changes]. // There is no destruction of the restraint upon the first and second changes of sexual characteristics — that is the meaning. These two rules are drawn from the <s>Kṣudrakas</s> (Minor Matters) on account of similarity. // (618) The arising [of restraint occurs] when [ordination] is being undertaken. // When ordination is being undertaken and there is a change of sexual characteristics, the restraint arises. // 'The sexual characteristics of one awaiting ordination change — is he to be declared ordained or unordained? He said: He is to be declared unordained. For a <s>bhikṣuṇī's</s> ordination and <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>-status must be sought from the <s>bhikṣus</s>' — this is the text here. // The illustration here is the change of a man's sexual characteristics. Due to the greater freedom from apprehension, the rule is different here. The one in the state of being ordained — the one observing the ordination — is included here, since a prior change would not be applicable to the assembly of mere <s>bhikṣus</s>. // (619) When there is no preceptor, [the restraint arises] for one who has [a preceptor]. // 'One who has' means one who has a preceptor. The restraint arises even without a preceptor. // (620) Even when his [preceptor] is unordained. // Even when the preceptor is unordained, does the restraint arise for one who has a preceptor? — // (621) Not when the one [undertaking ordination] knows his non-<s>bhikṣu</s> status. // The restraint does not arise for one who has a preceptor when the one undertaking [the ordination] knows the non-<s>bhikṣu</s> status — the unordained status or the fallen status — of his preceptor. The text here: 'One awaiting ordination is ordained by a preceptor who is a <s>steyasaṃvāsaka</s> (one living secretly in the <s>saṅgha</s>) — is he to be declared ordained or unordained? He said: If he knows "My preceptor is a <s>steyasaṃvāsaka</s>," he is to be declared unordained. If he does not know, he is to be declared ordained. Similarly with a preceptor who has previously incurred [a defeat]'...and so on... 'with a distracted householder as preceptor.' Now, even when there is no preceptor, the restraint arises — then how is it that when one knows his non-<s>bhikṣu</s> status, it does not arise? Because the intention [of the objection] is: since the fallen one knows, he is unaffected in morality, or morality is useless — therefore this arises. [But that is not so.] He does not know the non-preceptor status [as such]; therefore there is no contradiction with the non-arising here. // But what was stated — that when the preceptor is unordained, the restraint arises — this was stated with reference to the <s>saṅgha</s>: the restraint arises because the one undertaking [ordination] knows the unordained status of the <s>saṅgha</s>, not [merely] the one observing the ordination. // (622) Not when rejecting him. // Since the preceptor is the foundation of the restraint, in rejecting the preceptor there is no arising of the restraint. // The text here: 'One being ordained rejects the preceptor — is he to be declared ordained or unordained? He said: Unordained.' // (623) Not when the names of these two are not announced. // When the names of these two — the candidate and the preceptor — are not announced by the one undertaking [ordination] or by the procedure-performer, there is no arising of the restraint. // (624) Nor [when the name] of the <s>saṅgha</s>, which is its origin, [is not announced]. // When the name of the <s>saṅgha</s> is not announced by either the one undertaking or the procedure-performer — of the <s>saṅgha</s>, which is the origin, of that lineage — the restraint does not arise. // The text here: 'The one undertaking (

) prati trayaḥ pudgalāḥ anupasaṃpannāḥ, ātmano nāma na ācaṣṭe, upādhyāyasya nāma nācaṣṭe, upasaṃpadaṃ ca na jānāti" iti / karmakārakaṃ prati ayaṃ granthaḥ - "trayāṇāṃ nāma na parikīrtayati - upādhyāyasya, upasaṃpadāprekṣiṇaḥ, saṃghasya ca / upasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ, anupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ iti / [āha - anupasaṃpanno vaktavya iti] / apratyupasthāpanametad,
gṛhītatvena yadatra samādātuḥ ātmano nāmā 'nukīrtanam / saṃghasyaitad pratyupasthāpanam / anugṛhītatvena yat saṃghasyā nena nāmānudbhāvanam / yad karmakārakeṇa samādātuḥ tadviṣayatvasya upanīteḥ tadakaraṇam / yatsaṃghasya saṃghakartṛkatvasya upanīteḥ tadkaraṇam / yadupādhyāyasya karmakārakeṇa nāmā 'nudbhāvanaṃ, tadapi saṃghakartṛkatvasyaiva upanīteḥ akaraṇam / yasmāt yatra karmaṇi tatra saṃghasya kartṛtvapratipattiḥ, tato 'nyasya tatkarmaṇaḥ karaṇam / yadupādhyāyasya samādātrā nāmānudbhāvanaṃ, tad yasya karmaṇaḥ karaṇaṃ sopādhyāyakasya, na tatra tasya viṣayatvena pratyupasthānam / tadanutthānaṃ eṣāṃ nāmānudbhāvane saṃvarasya // (625) nā 'gārika-tīrthikadhvaje // pratyekaṃ dhvajaśabdasya parisamāptiḥ / āgārikadhvaje tīrthikadhvaje iti bahuvrīhiścātra samāsaḥ / āgārikadhvajo dhvajo yasya, tīrthikadhvajo dhvajo yasya / ābhyāṃ dhvajābhyāṃ gṛhītābhyāṃ na bhavati saṃvarasyotthānam / veṣaścātra dhvajaḥ // (626) na nagnakupita puṃphālinīṣu // saṃvarasyotthānaṃ ityanuṣaṅgaḥ / samādānato nagnībhūtasya tīrthikadhvajaḥ iti anenaiva saṃgrahāt / anyārthaṃ nagnagrahaṇam, pramuktapragrahatvaṃ asyāmavasthāyāṃ cittasya iti saṃvarasyānutthānam / kupitatve sthairyabhaṅgaḥ / puṃphāliṇīṃ tāvatā bhadantā upasaṃpādayanti, upasaṃpannā vaktavyā atha anupasaṃpannā? [āha] - anupasaṃpannā vaktavyā / upasaṃpādakāśca sātisārā iti / puṃphālinī puraḥ yatsaṃyogāt puruṣo mriyate // (627) na nimittaviparyayā 'nabhyupetau utkṣiptakasya // sa-dṛṣṭeḥ virati āśayasya saṃvarasaṃpattiḥ, tasmāt yena nimittena āpattyadarśanādinā - utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karmakṛtaṃ bhavati, tadviparyaya-anabhyupagame nāṣti saṃvarasya utthānam / nidarśanamatra utkṣiptakaḥ / sarvapraṇihiteṣu eṣa vidhiḥ / kalahakaraṇādi-āśayasyāpi avirati-āśayatvāt // (628) duṣkṛtamātrakaṃ apūrva-parvatāyām / vinā upāsakatvena śrāmaṇeratvopagatau, vinā śrāmaṇeratvena bhikṣutvopagatau duṣkṛtamātrakaṃ bhavati, na anutthānaṃ saṃvarasya // grantho 'tra - "āgārika-apravrajitakaṃ upasaṃpādayanti, upasaṃpanno vaktavyo 'nupasaṃpanno vaktavya ityāha - 'upasaṃpannaḥ, upālin, upasaṃpādakāśca āpadyante duṣkṛtā [patti]miti" // (629-630) ayāñcāyāmupādhyāyasya antarāyikayā 'praśne // ubhayatra atra duskṛtamātrakam, na anutthānaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) with respect to [the one undertaking ordination], three persons are unordained: [when] he does not declare his own name, does not declare the preceptor's name, and does not know the ordination.' This is the text regarding the procedure-performer: 'He does not announce the names of three — the preceptor, the one awaiting ordination, and the <s>saṅgha</s>. Is he to be declared ordained or unordained? [He said: Unordained.]' This is non-presentation. Through the acceptance [by the candidate], that which here is the announcement of the one undertaking [ordination] of his own name — this is the presentation to the <s>saṅgha</s>. Through the acceptance [by the <s>saṅgha</s>], that which is the non-announcement of the <s>saṅgha's</s> name by him. What is the non-performance by the procedure-performer regarding the candidate's connection with the relevant domain. What is the performance regarding the <s>saṅgha's</s> agency in the <s>saṅgha</s>-procedure. What is the non-announcement of the preceptor's name by the procedure-performer — that too is the non-performance of [establishing] the <s>saṅgha's</s> agency. For wherever there is a procedure, there the <s>saṅgha</s> has the capacity of agent; from that, another's performance of that procedure [follows]. What is the non-announcement of the preceptor's name by the one undertaking — that, since the procedure is for one having a preceptor, is not a presentation of him as its object [in that context]. The non-arising [of the restraint] for these [cases] is in the non-announcement of names. // (625) Not with the marks of a householder or a <s>tīrthika</s>. // The word 'mark' (<s>dhvaja</s>) applies to each separately: 'with the mark of a householder,' 'with the mark of a <s>tīrthika</s>' — and this is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound here. One whose mark is that of a householder; one whose mark is that of a <s>tīrthika</s>. When these two marks are adopted, the restraint does not arise. And here 'mark' means garb. // (626) Not in the case of the naked, the angry, or the <s>puṃphālinī</s>. // The continuation is: of the arising of the restraint. For one who has become naked through undertaking [a vow], this is included by the expression 'mark of a <s>tīrthika</s>.' The mention of 'naked' serves another purpose — in this state the mind has lost its hold, therefore the restraint does not arise. In the state of anger, stability is broken. As for a <s>puṃphālinī</s>: 'They ordain a <s>puṃphālinī</s> — is she to be declared ordained or unordained? [He said:] Unordained. And the ordainers incur a fault.' A <s>puṃphālinī</s> is [a woman] through whose sexual contact a man dies. // (627) Not when the reversal of grounds and the non-acceptance of one under suspension [are not present]. // The accomplishment of the restraint [requires] the intention of desisting from [wrong] views. Therefore, when the reversal of the grounds by which a formal act of suspension is performed — such as not seeing an offense — is not accepted, there is no arising of the restraint. The illustration here is the case of one under suspension. This rule applies to all [formal acts that are] established. Because the intention regarding quarrel-making etc. is also an intention of non-desisting. // (628) Only a minor offense (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) in the case of one who arrives [at a stage] without the preceding [stage]. // When one attains the status of novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>) without [first becoming] a lay-follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), or when one attains <s>bhikṣu</s>-status without [first becoming] a novice, there is only a minor offense, not a non-arising of the restraint. // The text here: 'They ordain a householder who has not gone forth — is he to be declared ordained or unordained? He said: Ordained, <s>Upālin</s>, but the ordainers incur a minor offense.' // (629–630) When the preceptor has not been requested, and when there is no inquiry about impediments. // In both cases here there is only a minor offense, not a non-arising (
<s>VinSū</s> 56

children.text:
) saṃvarasyetyanuṣaraṅgaḥ // (631) pratijñāne 'sya asato dāne // asato iti asaṃvidyamānasya, samādātra antarāyikasya 'asti me 'ntarāyikam' iti pratijñāne saṃvarasya dāne duṣkṛtamāṭrakaṃ, na anutthānam // nidāneṣvatra granthaḥ - "antarāyikaiḥ tāvat bhadanta dharmaiḥ samanvāgatam, 'samanvāgato 'sti' iti vadantaṃ upasaṃpādayanti / upasaṃpanno vaktavyo 'nupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ, āha - 'upasampannaḥ' upasaṃpādakāstu sātisārāḥ" iti / tad atra antarāyikaṃ abhipretaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate, yadvidhe tu ahamupasaṃpannaḥ // (632) na puruṣānukṛtitvaṃ striyā, stryanukṛtitvaṃ ca puruṣasya vyaṃjanāntaraprakāraḥ // nātra anutthānaṃ saṃvarasya, etatpradarśanaṃ - vyañjanāntarasya prakāratvāt atrotthānaṃ na syāt / na caitadeṣa bhavati
- //
children.translated_text: ) of the restraint — the continuation. // (631) When one who does not have [an impediment] falsely declares [that he has one], in the giving [of ordination]. // 'Who does not have' means one in whom [the impediment] is not found. When one falsely declares 'I have an impediment' and the restraint is given to the one undertaking [ordination], there is only a minor offense, not a non-arising. // In the <s>Nidānas</s> the text is: 'He is endowed with impediment-producing conditions, Venerable Ones. They ordain one who says "I am endowed [with impediments]." Is he to be declared ordained or unordained? He said: Ordained. But the ordainers incur a fault.' In this case, the impediment intended is understood [as absent]; but in the case of one of the type 'I am ordained' — // (632) A woman's imitation of a man, or a man's [imitation] of a woman, is a different type of [change in] sexual characteristics (<s>vyañjana</s>). // Here there is no non-arising of the restraint. This demonstration [shows] — because it is a type of change in characteristics, the arising should not be [negated] here. And this [case] does not constitute [a genuine change] — //

body.translated_text: (615) There is no domain for restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) for one reborn in a non-human destiny or for an <s>Uttarakauravaka</s> (one from the northern continent of <s>Uttarakuru</s>). // One who has been reborn in a destiny other than the human destiny, or even one in the human destiny who is an <s>Uttarakauravaka</s> — for these there is no restraint.
(b) The state of being challenged (<s>ākṣiptatva</s>). //

body.text: (633) ākṣiptatvamasya hastacchinnādinā / asya puruṣasya anukṛtitvasya hastacchinnāḥ pādacchinnā ityādinā ākṣiptatvam, ākṣiptatvācca duṣkṛtāmā[trami]tyuktaṃ bhavati // (634) pāpalakṣaṇa-bhinnakalpadvīpāntarajayoḥ // anayorapi hastacchinnādinā ākṣiptatvamityarthaḥ // "pāpalakṣaṇaṃ upasaṃpādayanti" [iti] yāvadupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ / bhikṣavastu upasaṃpādakāḥ āpadyante duṣkṛtāmiti" pāpalakṣaṇe granthaḥ // [nidāna]-dvīpāntarajo 'pi granthaḥ - jambudvīpakā bhikṣavaḥ pūrvavidehakamupasaṃpādayanti, upasapanno vaktavyaḥ '.......... yāvad - 'upasaṃpannaḥ, upālin' / 'upasaṃpadakāstu sātisārāḥ' / [iti] vistareṇa cakrapeyālaṃ karvatyam // saṃsthāna-pramāṇa-daśābhedo manuṣyāṇāṃ yatra dvīpe tanmātravyudāśasavaraṃ atra dvīpagrahaṇaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate / etadatra bhinnakalpagrahaṇena viśeṣitamukhādibhedo 'pi atra kalpabhedo 'bhipretaḥ / evaṃ ca ekadvīpakānāmapi eṣa mukha-karṇaprāvaraṇādīnāṃ pratikṣiptatvaṃ veditavyam // (635) ekanakha-samudralekha-pakṣahata-liṅgaśiro-gulmakeśa-antarbahirdvi-kubja-ṣaṭsahitā 'naṅguli-pakṣma-nakula-kiṃpila-viparīta-milita-śikya-kaśmīlita-akṣākṣa-akṣiśāla-śantra-dardru-vicarcika-pīta-avadāta-rakta-nāḍīkarṇa-kaṇḍu-piṇḍa-sthūlakacchu-aṇḍalāṅgūlapraticchanna-mūḍha-ajihva-ekahastapāda-[ahastapāda]-nīlakeśa-hastyaśvaśvagomeṣamṛgamatsyāhi-dīrghabahuśīrṣa-tālakaṅṭhaśūleryāpathacchinnebhyaśca anābādhikānāṃ, glānena ca itareṣām // ekanakhādīnāṃ ca adhuktānāṃ [hasta]chinnādinā ākṣiptatvaṃ, itaresāṃ tu ābādhikānāṃ, glānena 'mā 'si glānaḥ' ityanena ākṣiptatvaṃ ityarthaḥ // ekanakho, yasya ekameva nakham / samudralekho, yasya mudrāyuktamiva lekhaṃ śarīrāvayavaḥ / pakṣaheto, yasya ekaṃ pārśvaṃ śuṣkam / liṅgaśirā, yasya liṅgākāraṃ śiraḥ / gulmakeśo (

children.translated_text: <s>Vinayasūtra</s> 57

) — one whose hair stands in clumps like a buffoon's. 'Inward, outward, and dual hunchback' — the word 'hunchback' (<s>kubja</s>) applies to each individually: inwardly hunchbacked, outwardly hunchbacked, inwardly-and-outwardly hunchbacked. This is stated elsewhere as: 'one-eyed, crippled, hunchbacked, and deformed' — but here it is for the purpose of showing the subdivisions. 'Six, fused, and no fingers' — the word 'finger' (<s>aṅguli</s>) applies to each individually: six-fingered, fused-fingered, and fingerless. Six-fingeredness, fused-fingeredness, and mere fingerlessness. By 'no finger' here, the inclusion of one with webbed fingers [like a fan] is implied. 'Eyelash, mongoose, owl, reversed, fused, drooping, squinting, and rolling — eyes': the word 'eye' (<s>akṣa</s>) applies to each individually — eyelash-eyed, mongoose-eyed, owl-eyed, reversed-eyed, fused-eyed, drooping-eyed, squinting-eyed, rolling-eyed. 'Eyelash-eyed' (<s>pakṣmākṣa</s>): one in whose eye, within the fold of skin, eyelashes grow [inward]. [Mongoose-eyed (<s>nakulākṣa</s>): one whose eye is like a mongoose's.] 'Owl-eyed' (<s>kiṃpilākṣa</s>) [also called] 'copper-eyed' — due to [the color of] the eyes; or 'demon-eyed' or 'similar-eyed.' 'Reversed-eyed' (<s>viparītākṣa</s>): one for whom the part of the eye near the outer corner is at the nose, and the part near the nose is at the outer corner. 'Fused-eyed' (<s>militākṣa</s>): one whose eyes, with the nose-bridge absent, are joined to each other. 'Drooping-eyed' (<s>śikyākṣa</s>): one whose eyes hang down excessively like a basket. 'Squinting-eyed' (<s>kaśmīlitākṣa</s>): one whose eyelashes and hair have fallen out and whose eye-margin oozes blood-like fluid. 'Rolling-eyed' (<s>akṣākṣa</s>): one whose eyes [roll like] dice. 'Eye-wide, eye-spotted, eye-ringworm, eye-eczema' — the word 'eye' (<s>akṣi</s>) applies to each individually: wide-eyed, spotted-eyed, ringworm-eyed, eczema-eyed. 'Wide-eyed' (<s>akṣiśāla</s>): one whose eyes are excessively wide. 'Yellow, white, red, tube-like — ears' — the word 'ear' (<s>karṇa</s>) applies to each individually: yellow-eared, white-eared, red-eared, tube-eared. 'Itching, lump, coarse — scabs' — the word 'scab' (<s>kacchu</s>) applies to each individually: itching-scab, lump-scab, coarse-scab. 'Testes-covering-tail' (<s>aṇḍalāṅgūlapraticchanna</s>): one whose tail [i.e., posterior] is covered by the testes. 'Confused' (<s>mūḍha</s>): by this, [the case of] one who does not understand ordination is included. 'Tongueless' (<s>ajihva</s>): one who lacks a tongue. Since 'mute and deaf' includes, under 'mute,' one who, though having a tongue, is unable to speak — being tongueless is for one who actually lacks a tongue, since 'tongueless' has been stated [separately]. 'One hand, one foot' — the word 'one' (<s>eka</s>) applies to 'hand' and 'foot' individually: one-handed, one-footed; and handless-and-footless. 'Blue-haired' (<s>nīlakeśa</s>): 'blue' here means that which has not become green; therefore, blue is covered by the mention of 'green.' 'Elephant, horse, dog, cow, sheep, deer, fish, snake, long, many — headed' — the word 'headed' (<s>śīrṣa</s>) applies to each individually: elephant-headed, horse-headed, dog-headed, cow-headed, sheep-headed, deer-headed, fish-headed, snake-headed, long-headed, many-headed. As for 'all-blue, all-yellow, all-red, all-white' — this reading also [appears]; these are covered by the statement of the four [possible] skin colors. 'Goitered, pain-afflicted, gait-impaired' [are also listed]. (636) Of a thief and a brigand. The continuation is 'inclusion.' The general characteristic of evil conduct [connects them]. But is there not no distinction between these? — There is, for a thief (<s>caura</s>) —
<s>Vinayasūtra</s> 58

children.text: ) saghṛṇaḥ paraharaṇaḥ, sarveṇa sarvaṃ yadbhūyasā yasya vā abhiprāṇātipātapravarttā / dasyuśca acaurabhūtaḥ nirghṛṇo vadhyaghātakādiḥ / tasmāt pṛthaktvamevāsya bhavati //
children.translated_text: ) — with compassion, takes others' [property]; [he is] one who for the most part, or whose primary inclination, engages in stealing. But a brigand (<s>dasyu</s>), who is not a thief, is merciless — an executioner of condemned persons and the like. Therefore, the distinction between them indeed exists.

body.translated_text: (633) Its inclusion [is established] through the [case of] one whose hand is cut off, etc. This person — the imitator — is included through 'those whose hand is cut off, foot cut off' and so forth; and from this inclusion, it is stated that [the offense for ordaining such a person is] merely a <s>duṣkṛta</s> (minor wrong). (634) For those with evil marks (<s>pāpalakṣaṇa</s>) and those from [a continent] of different customs (<s>bhinnakalpadvīpāntaraja</s>). For these two also, the inclusion [is established] through the [case of] one whose hand is cut off, etc. — this is the meaning. 'They ordain one with evil marks' — up to: 'he is to be declared fully ordained. But the <s>bhikṣus</s> who perform the ordination incur a <s>duṣkṛta</s>' — this is the text regarding one with evil marks. The text regarding one from another continent also [states]: '<s>Jambudvīpa</s> <s>bhikṣus</s> ordain a <s>Pūrvavideha</s> person; he is to be declared fully ordained... up to: "He is fully ordained, <s>Upālin</s>." "But the ordainers are to be reproved."' — and so forth; the full cycle should be elaborated. The mention of 'continent' here applies to [continents] where humans differ from those [of this continent] in form, size, and condition — [with] only that much difference being the limit. And here, by the mention of 'different customs,' even differences in facial coverings etc. are intended as differences in custom. Thus, even among those of the same continent, the prohibition of face-coverings, ear-coverings, and the like should be understood. (635) For those with one nail (<s>ekanakha</s>), sea-marks (<s>samudralekha</s>), half-paralysis (<s>pakṣahata</s>), phallus-shaped head (<s>liṅgaśiras</s>), bush-like hair (<s>gulmakeśa</s>), inward hunchback, outward hunchback, dual hunchback; six fingers, fused fingers, no fingers; eyelash-eyes, mongoose-eyes, owl-eyes, reversed eyes, fused eyes, drooping eyes, squinting eyes, rolling eyes; wide eyes, spotted eyes, ringworm eyes, eczema eyes; yellow ears, white ears, red ears, tube-like ears; itching scabs, lump scabs, coarse scabs; those whose testes cover the tail; the confused, the tongueless, the one-handed, the one-footed, [the handless and footless]; blue-haired; those with heads [shaped like those of] elephants, horses, dogs, cows, sheep, deer, fish, or snakes; long-headed, many-headed; those with goiter, pain, and impaired gait — for those among these who are not ill, [ordination is prohibited]; and for the remaining [conditions that are] illnesses, by one who is sick. For those beginning with 'one-nailed' and others not mentioned, the inclusion [is established] through 'one whose hand is cut off' etc.; but for the remaining [conditions that are] illnesses, the inclusion [is established] through the [question] 'Are you ill?' — this is the meaning. 'One-nailed' (<s>ekanakha</s>): one who has only a single nail. 'Sea-marked' (<s>samudralekha</s>): one whose body parts have lines as if stamped with a seal. 'Half-paralyzed' (<s>pakṣahata</s>): one whose one side is withered. 'Phallus-headed' (<s>liṅgaśiras</s>): one whose head is phallus-shaped. 'Bush-haired' (<s>gulmakeśa</s>) —
(c) Permission (<s>anujñā</s>)

body.text: (637) pitṛ-vat pitrāśayatve anujñāyāṃ rājā // pitrāśayatvena rājñā 'nujñātaḥ pitṛbhyāmevānujñāto draṣṭavyaḥ / rājānujñayā pravrājite [adoṣo] draṣṭavyaḥ iti bhāvaḥ // (638) parigṛhītroḥ anujñāna-dhāraṇā-ārocaneṣu pitṛtvam // asatyapi janakatve mātāpitṛparigraheṇa avasthitayoḥ anujñāne saptāhadhāraṇe saṃghe ca ārocane [mātā-]pitṛtvaṃ, na janakayoreva parigṛhītṛtvena avasthitayoḥ ityarthaḥ / "putrakṛtakaṃ tāvat, bhadanta, upasaṃpādayanti, kasya sakāśā[dava]sāritavyaḥ? - yasya putratvamupagataḥ, evaṃ dhītikṛtikā yasya dhītitvaṃ upagatikā" - ityatra granthaḥ // (639) na amanuṣyagatikayoḥ // anujñānadhāraṇā 'rocaneṣu pitṛtvaṃ ityanuṣaṅgaḥ // "yasya tāvat, bhadanta, mātāpitarau kālagatu bhavataḥ, tiryagyonigatau vā, tasya keśāvaropaṇāya sarvasaṃgho 'valokayitavyaḥ? - no hīdaṃ, upālin" ityatra granthaḥ // (640) na ataḥ ānantaryotthāṇam // amanuṣyagatikābhyāṃ pitṛbhyām ānantaryotthānam // (641) janakābhyāmetad, parivṛttavyaṃjanābhyāmapi // apuṃstvamapi mātṛgatātve 'pi tuṣka strītvaṃ utthānamānantaryasya // (642) etad-kṛtvaṃ mātṛghātakādau tattvam // etatkṛtvaṃ ānantaryakṛtvaṃ, yad māṭṛghātakādeḥ pravrājanaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ tatra ānantaryakṛtvaṃ tattu pratipattavyam / ānantaryakārī na pravrājyaḥ ityevaṃ puna stad / na sarvamātṛghāṭako na pravrājya ityevaṃ ca / tiryagyonigatamātṛghātakasya apratiṣiddhaṃ bhavati pravrājanam //
body.translated_text: (637) The king, when [acting] with parental intention, [serves] like a parent in granting permission. When the king grants permission with the attitude of a parent, he should be regarded as equivalent to the parents [in granting permission for ordination]. When ordination is performed with the king's permission, [there is] no fault — this is the meaning. (638) For those taken in [by adoptive parents], the parental status [applies] in matters of permission, the seven-day retention, and announcement [to the <s>saṅgha</s>]. Even without biological parentage, for those established by the embrace of [adoptive] mother and father, the parental status [applies] in granting permission, in the seven-day retention [of the candidate], and in the announcement to the <s>saṅgha</s> — not [only] for the biological parents established in the role of guardians — this is the meaning. The text here is: 'Now, <s>Bhadanta</s>, they ordain an adopted son — from whom should he obtain release? From the one to whom he has entered into sonship. Likewise an adopted daughter — from the one to whom she has entered into daughter-status.' (639) Not for those [parents] gone to non-human realms. The continuation is: 'the parental status in matters of permission, retention, and announcement.' The text here is: 'Now, <s>Bhadanta</s>, when one's mother and father have died, or have gone to an animal birth — should the entire <s>saṅgha</s> be consulted for his tonsure? — No, <s>Upālin</s>.' (640) No arising of a grave offense (<s>ānantarya</s>) from these. From parents gone to non-human realms, [there is] no arising of a grave offense [from killing them]. (641) This [applies] to biological [parents], and also to those whose [sex] marks have changed. Even lack of masculinity [arising from] a mother's having become [male], or femaleness [of a father] — [there is still] the arising of a grave offense. (642) The commission of a grave offense is the relevant factor in the case of a mother-killer etc. — that is the [true] criterion. 'Commission of a grave offense' means the commission of an <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous act). That the ordination of a mother-killer etc. is prohibited — therein, the commission of a grave offense is what should be considered as the criterion. 'One who has committed a grave offense should not be ordained' — thus it is. Not 'every mother-killer should not be ordained' — for the ordination of one who has killed a mother gone to an animal birth is not prohibited.
(d) Miscellaneous (<s>saṃkīrṇa</s>)

body.text: kasmin bhikṣuṇyāṃ kṛte bhikṣuṇīdūṣakatvaṃ jātaṃ bhavati, bhikṣuṇyā 'pi bhikṣudūṣakatvaṃ bhavati, kenārthena etadubhayamityāha - // (643) dūṣakatvaṃ abrahmacaryeṇa svādayatoḥ, aparājitatve // "kiyatā, bhadanta, bhikṣuṇīdūṣako vaktavyaḥ? - yena abrahmacaryeṇa, [upālin], bhikṣuṇī dūṣitā bhavati" iti granthaḥ / kiṃ yattaccetasoḥ asyotthānamityāha? - svadayatoḥ / gamya 'pi dūṣakatvasyosthānaṃ, gantaryapi ityasya saṃdarśanārthaṃ atra dvivacanam / no tu sahite pratiyogisvādanena dūṣakatvasya utthānam, ityasya na hi anya-pradoṣeṇa anyasya saṃbaṃdhaḥ, iti anaṅgatvaṃ atra pratiyogisvādasya / vītarāgadūṣaṇe ca dūṣakatvānutthānaprasaṃgāt / 'chandaśaḥ' iti yadvacanaṃ, eṣo 'tra āgamaḥ / svecchayā ityasya arthaḥ / pārājitatve 'pi bhikṣu-bhikṣuṇītvaṃ vidyate kim, tadavasthayoḥ nā 'pyanayoḥ dūṣaṇe dūṣakatvamityatra (

children.translated_text: [VinSū 59]

children.text:
) āha - aparājitatve / grantho 'tra - "aṣṭau tāvat, bhadanta, pudgalā pratyekavastubhīḥ bhikṣuṇīṃ dūṣayanti / duṣṭā sā bhikṣuṇī vaktavyā? duṣṭā, upālin, vaktavyā / katarāḥ tatra pudgalā bhikṣuṇī-dūṣakā vaktavyāḥ? - āha, na kaściditi / nipātane vā āmarṣaṇe vā aparājitatvaṃ bhikṣuṇyā iti hi etad adūṣakatva-vijñānam / kathaṃ tarhi? - anyenārthena nipatitāyāṃ, nikubjayāṃ vā, asvīkurvatyāṃ, āmarṣaṇa-parāmarṣana-saṃpraveśane, nipātyāpi asvīkāre tayā nipātanasya / svayaṃ vā saṃspṛśantyā puruṣagātraṃ, puruṣasyopakrāntiḥ // (644) arhatvaṃ pravrajyopasaṃpadoḥ upagatau puṃstvasya hīnāyāṃ yoṣiti // śikṣāṃ pratyākhyāya hīnāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ striyāṃ vyaṃjanaparivṛttyā puṃstvogatau arhatvaṃ pravrajyopasaṃpadoḥ / na-strītvāvasthāyāṃ iva anarhatvaṃ ityarthaḥ // (645) asādhāraṇaṃ ca pārājayikaṃ adhyācaritavatyām // 'arhatvaṃ pravrajyopasaṃpadoḥ upagatau puṃstvasya hīnāyāṃ yoṣiti' - ityanubandhaḥ // (646) āvāsikānāṃ strīupasaṃpādane aṅgatvaṃ // poṣadhavastu atra granthaḥ - "yaduktaṃ bhagavatā bhikṣuṇī bhiḥ bhikṣūṇāmantike bhikṣuṇībhāvaḥ paryeṣitavyaḥ iti katamesāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ āvāsika-naivāsikānāṃ, upālin", iti / tatsthānagatā vāsasthaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ upaniśritya bhikṣuṇīnāṃ vāsaḥ / tataḥ kālena kālaṃ avavāda-anuśāsanīmārgaṇāt, na ca niśrayātikramo yuktaḥ ityetad vijñānam / āvāsikatvamevātra viropitataratvena
viśiṣyamāṇaṃ naivāsikatvaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate // (647) dhvaṃso bhavatvasya [utsṛ]ṣṭau // bhavadbhāvye bhavatvaṃ jāyamānatvamityarthaḥ / gṛhyamāṇe saṃvare tasya saṃvarasya yadbhavatvaṃ tasya tadavasthasya utsṛṣṭau pratyākhyānādinā utsarge dhvaṃso bhavati / āvedha eṣa saṃvarasya yajjāyamānatvam / na ca āneghasya pratyudāvṛttiḥ laṅghanādau dṛśyate / tasmāt, na bhavatyasyā 'jāyamānatve saṃvarasya pratyudāvṛttiḥ iti yo manyeta tannābhinivṛttyartha etatsūtram / muktakeṣu atra granthaḥ - "upasaṃpannastābat, upālin, gṛhitvaṃ pratijānāno anupasaṃpanno vaktavyaḥ / prāgeva upasaṃpadya māna iti // pṛcchā prāyaṃ pravrajyāvastugatam //
children.translated_text: he says: '[provided they are] un-defeated' (<s>aparājitatve</s>). The text here [states]: 'Suppose, <s>Bhadanta</s>, eight persons individually defile a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> with separate objects. Is that <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> to be called defiled?' 'She is to be called defiled, <s>Upālin</s>.' 'Which persons among them are to be called defilors of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>?' — He said: 'None.' Whether by being thrown down or by being touched, the un-defeated status of the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> — this indeed is the criterion for non-defiler-status. How then? — When she has fallen for another purpose, or when she is bent over, or when she does not consent, in the case of touching, handling, and penetration, even when thrown down, [there is] non-consent on her part to the throwing down. Or when she herself touches a man's body, [if there is] the man's advance. (644) There is eligibility for ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>) when masculinity is attained, for a woman who has been [previously] degraded. When a woman who has renounced the training and been degraded, through the reversal of sexual characteristics attains masculinity — there is eligibility for ordination and full ordination. The meaning is: [there is] not ineligibility as in the state of womanhood. (645) And an uncommon <s>pārājika</s> (defeat) offense [applies] to one who has practiced [unchaste conduct]. 'There is eligibility for ordination and full ordination when masculinity is attained, for a woman who has been degraded' — this is the continuation. (646) The resident [<s>bhikṣus</s>] have a component role in the full ordination of women. The text here is from the <s>Poṣadhavastu</s>: 'As the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "The <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> should seek the status of <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> from the <s>bhikṣus</s>" — of which <s>bhikṣus</s>? The resident or the non-resident? <s>Upālin</s>' — [the answer:] the <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> reside depending upon the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> dwelling in that place. Therefore, from time to time, they seek instruction and admonition, and it is not proper to transgress the shelter-relationship — this is the understanding. The resident status here, being more established, is distinguished, while non-resident status is subordinate. (647) The dissolution [of the precepts occurs] upon renunciation of the state of being. 'The state of being' means the state of coming into existence, i.e., being born — this is the meaning. When the precepts are being taken, the 'state of being' of those precepts — of those in that state — upon renunciation, i.e., relinquishment through formal declaration, there is dissolution. This 'state of being' (<s>bhavatva</s>) is the vitality (<s>āvedha</s>) of the precepts — the state of coming into being. And the reversal of the undamaged [precepts] is not observed in [cases of mere] transgression and so forth. Therefore, one who thinks 'for one whose precepts have not come into non-being, there is no reversal of the precepts' — this <s>sūtra</s> is not for the purpose of [supporting] that fixation. The text from the <s>Muktaka</s> [states]: 'One who is fully ordained, <s>Upālin</s>, and claims householder-status — he is to be declared unordained. How much more so one who is [only] being ordained.' The matters that are mostly in the form of questions pertain to the <s>Pravrajyāvastu</s>.

body.translated_text: Under what circumstances does the status of 'defiler of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>' (<s>bhikṣuṇīdūṣakatva</s>) arise when [an act] is committed against a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, and does the status of 'defiler of a <s>bhikṣu</s>' also arise for the <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>? For what purpose is this dual [designation]? — He says: (643) The status of 'defiler' [arises through] unchaste conduct (<s>abrahmacārya</s>), when both consent, [provided they are] un-defeated (<s>aparājita</s>). The text [states]: 'To what extent, <s>Bhadanta</s>, is one to be called a defiler of a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>?' — 'By whatever unchaste conduct, <s>Upālin</s>, a <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> is defiled.' What mental state produces the arising of this [status]? — He says: 'when both consent' (<s>svādayatoḥ</s>). The arising of defiler-status [occurs] for the one approached (<s>gamya</s>) as well as for the one approaching (<s>gantar</s>) — to show this, the dual number is used here. However, the arising of defiler-status does not [occur] when the counterpart consents under coercion — for the corruption of one is not connected with the corruption of another — thus the consent of the counterpart is irrelevant here. And because in the case of defiling one who is free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>), the absurd consequence of non-arising of defiler-status [would follow]. The statement 'willingly' (<s>chandaśaḥ</s>) — this is the scriptural authority here; its meaning is 'by one's own will.' Even in the state of being defeated (<s>pārājita</s>), does the status of <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> still exist? In the defilement of those two in that state, is defiler-status [established]? On this point,
In the commentary on the <s>Vinaya</s> [composed from] his own explanation, the <s>Pravrajyāvastu</s> (Chapter on Going Forth) is concluded.
